definition_zh: 肉；食用肉；（果实或坚果的）可食部分；实质；要旨
definition_en: the flesh of animals eaten as food, the soft edible part inside fruit or nuts, or the central substance of something
core_image: 一块放在砧板上的肉，旁边是敲开的坚果，露出里面饱满的果仁
scene: 冬天的炖锅在灶上咕嘟作响，屋里飘着香料味。 She added a little salt to the meat and left it to simmer.
sceneCN: 这里是「供食用的肉」（第 1 个义项：动物肉作为食物）；句意为她往肉里加了一点盐，让它慢慢炖。

derivatives.zh: 由 meat 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「多肉的；内容丰富的」
由 meat 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无肉的」
由 meat 与 ball 复合而成，义为「肉丸」

senses.title: Animal flesh used as food
senses.definition: the flesh of animals, especially cattle, pigs and sheep, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 尤指牛、猪、羊等动物供人食用的肉
senses.example: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
senses.exampleCN: 屠夫把肉切成薄片。
senses.why: Old English mete meant food of any kind; as other foods took their own names, the general word narrowed onto the flesh sold at a butcher's stall.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mete 泛指任何食物；随着其他食物各自有了名字，这个宽泛的词就收窄到肉铺案板上出售的肉。

senses.title: The edible soft part of fruit or nuts
senses.definition: the soft or fleshy part inside a fruit, nut or shell that can be eaten
senses.definitionCN: 水果、坚果或壳内可供食用的柔软部分
senses.example: Crack the shell and scoop out the meat of the walnut.
senses.exampleCN: 敲开壳，把核桃仁挖出来。
senses.why: The idea of the edible inside of a thing was already present in food, so the word was extended to the part of a nut or fruit worth eating.
senses.whyCN: 「某物内部可食的部分」这一想法本就包含在「食物」里，于是词义被扩展到坚果或水果里值得吃的那一部分。

senses.title: The central substance of an idea or text
senses.definition: the most important part or central content of an argument, book or plan
senses.definitionCN: 论点、书或计划中最重要的部分、核心内容
senses.example: The meat of the report is in its final three pages.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的要旨就在最后三页。
senses.why: If flesh is what fills a body, then the substantial part of a text can be called its meat, with the rest treated as bone or wrapping.
senses.whyCN: 如果肉是填满身体的东西，那么一篇文章的实质部分也可以叫它的 meat，其余部分则被看成骨头或包装。

senses.title: Food of any kind, in older usage
senses.definition: solid food in general, the older sense still visible in a few fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 泛指固体食物，这一较古的词义仍残留在少数固定短语中
senses.example: In older English, meat could mean any food a household stored.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的英语里，meat 可以指一户人家储存的任何食物。
senses.why: This is the original sense; it survives mainly in old texts and in the fixed phrase meat and drink, while everyday usage keeps only the flesh sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的词义；它主要残存在旧文本与固定短语 meat and drink 里，日常用法只保留了「肉」这一义项。

intro.en: Meat began as a general word for food and narrowed to animal flesh, a shift whose exact cause is not settled.
intro.cn: meat 起初是泛指食物的词，后来收窄为动物肉，这一变化的确切原因尚无定论。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *matiz meant food, and its earlier origin is uncertain; no reliable Latin cognate is recorded.
items.cn: 重构名词 *matiz 意为食物，其更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.en: Old English mete meant food or nourishment of any kind, not flesh in particular.
items.cn: 古英语 mete 泛指食物或营养，并不专指肉。

items.en: Middle English kept the broad sense, and meat could still name bread, fruit or drink in the same sentence.
items.cn: 中古英语保留宽泛的词义，meat 仍可与面包、水果或饮料并列。

items.en: Usage narrowed towards animal flesh, though scholars do not agree on a single cause for the change.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄到动物肉，不过学者对变化的确切原因并无一致结论。

items.en: The flesh sense dominates, while the older idea survives in compounds and in the figurative sense of substance.
items.cn: 「肉」的义项占主导，较古的词义则保存在复合词与「实质」的比喻义里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the flesh family and one word that merely sounds the same; the near-meaning group collects names for flesh and for kinds of meat.
note.cn: 形近组收「肉」这一族词，外加一个只是读音相同的词；近义组收表示肉与各种肉类的词。

entries.definition: Full of meat, or rich and substantial in content.
entries.definitionCN: 多肉的；内容丰富的。

entries.definition: A ball of minced meat cooked in sauce or soup.
entries.definitionCN: 用肉末做成、在酱汁或汤里煮的丸子。

entries.definition: Made or eaten without meat.
entries.definitionCN: 不含肉或以无肉方式食用的。

entries.definition: To come together with someone; only the sound and spelling are close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人会面；只是读音和拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The soft body tissue of a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物身上的软组织。

entries.definition: Meat from cattle, a specific kind of red meat.
entries.definitionCN: 牛肉，一种具体的红肉。

entries.definition: Meat from pigs.
entries.definitionCN: 猪肉。

entries.definition: Wild animals hunted for food, or their meat.
entries.definitionCN: 供食用的野味或其肉。

normalIntro.en: The word started wide and ended narrow, and the old width still shows in a few compounds and in the sense of substance.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从宽泛起步、以狭窄收场，旧日的宽泛仍体现在少数复合词与「实质」义里。

normal.en: Old English mete was a general word for food, so the ancestor of meat had nothing to do with animals.
normal.cn: 古英语 mete 是泛指食物的词，所以 meat 的祖先与动物无关。

normal.en: The narrowing to flesh happened gradually, and nobody can point to one single cause.
normal.cn: 收窄为「肉」是逐渐发生的，没有人能指出唯一的原因。

normal.en: The adjective meaty adds -y, and meatless adds -less, two small endings that show the flesh sense clearly.
normal.cn: 形容词 meaty 加 -y，meatless 加 -less，两个小后缀清楚显示了「肉」的义项。

normal.en: Meatball is a plain compound: meat plus ball, the shape named directly.
normal.cn: meatball 是直白的复合词：meat 加 ball，直接以形状命名。

normal.en: The meat of a walnut or the meat of an argument keeps the old idea of the edible or substantial inside.
normal.cn: 核桃的 meat 或论点的 meat，都保留了「内部可食或实质部分」的旧想法。

abstract.en: Picture a butcher's block: the word food shrank until it fit exactly on that block.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肉铺的砧板：food 这个词不断缩小，直到正好落在砧板上。

abstract.en: Every language has words that start wide and end narrow, and meat is one of the clearest examples.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都有由宽变窄的词，meat 就是最清楚的例子之一。

abstract.en: Cut a nut open and the same word appears again, this time for the good part inside.
abstract.cn: 把坚果切开，同一个词又出现了，这次指里面最好的那部分。

examples.en: She added a little salt to the meat and left it to simmer.
examples.cn: 她往肉里加了一点盐，让它慢慢炖。

examples.en: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
examples.cn: 屠夫把肉切成薄片。

examples.en: The meat of the report is in its final three pages.
examples.cn: 报告的要旨就在最后三页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蜜特」——烤肉抹上蜜特别香；记住 meat 是肉，也可指实质。

root: 古英语 mete（泛指食物），出自原始日耳曼语 *matiz（食物），更早来源不确定，未见可靠的拉丁同族词；词义后来收窄为「动物肉」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the edible part of a body; the senses move from animal flesh to the inside of a nut and finally to the substance of an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是身体上可食的部分；义项从动物肉移到坚果内部，最后移到论点的实质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut of meat on a block beside a cracked nut showing its kernel.
core.cn: 核心意象：砧板上的一块肉，旁边是敲开的坚果，露出果仁。

branches.en: a butcher slicing a joint on a block
branches.cn: 屠夫在砧板上切一大块肉

branches.en: a cracked walnut with its kernel exposed
branches.cn: 敲开的核桃露出果仁

branches.en: a reader underlining the last pages
branches.cn: 读者在最后几页画线

branches.en: an old kitchen storing bread and drink
branches.cn: 老厨房里存着面包和饮料

branches.en: the same word for a steak and for an argument
branches.cn: 同一个词既指牛排也指论点

intro.en: The entry is supported by an Old English food noun, its Germanic source, two productive suffixes and two everyday compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词条由古英语的食物名词、它的日耳曼语来源、两个能产后缀和两个日常复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for meat; Latin carō, the word for flesh, is a synonym rather than a relative.
latinIntro.cn: meat 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 carō 表示「肉」，只是近义词而非同源词。

definition_zh: 垃圾；废物；废话
definition_en: waste material that is thrown away; things of poor quality; foolish talk or ideas
core_image: 一堆被丢弃、不再有用的东西
scene: 请把厨房里的垃圾拿出去。 Please take the rubbish out of the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 rubbish 是「垃圾」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把厨房里的垃圾拿出去。

derivatives.zh: 劣质的；垃圾般的
垃圾桶
垃圾场

senses.title: Waste material
senses.definition: waste material that is thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 被丢弃的废弃材料
senses.example: The bin was full of rubbish.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾桶里装满了垃圾。
senses.why: The core sense is useless waste.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是无用的废弃物。

senses.title: Poor quality things
senses.definition: things that are of very poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 质量极差的东西
senses.example: The film was pure rubbish.
senses.exampleCN: 那部电影简直一无是处。
senses.why: Waste material becomes a judgment on things.
senses.whyCN: 废弃物变成了对事物的评价。

senses.title: Foolish talk
senses.definition: foolish talk or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢的话或想法
senses.example: Don't talk rubbish about her.
senses.exampleCN: 别乱说她的是非。
senses.why: Worthless things become worthless words.
senses.whyCN: 没有价值的东西变成没有价值的话。

intro.en: Rubbish comes from Middle English robous, rubble or waste.
intro.cn: rubbish 源自中古英语 robous，意为碎石、废料。

items.en: Robous names broken stone and waste.
items.cn: robous 指碎石与废料。

items.en: Related forms describe rubble from buildings.
items.cn: 相关词形描述建筑物产生的碎石。

items.en: Rubbish broadens to household waste.
items.cn: rubbish 扩大到家庭垃圾。

items.en: Rubbish also means worthless things.
items.cn: rubbish 也指毫无价值的东西。

items.en: Talk rubbish is a common phrase.
items.cn: talk rubbish 成为常用说法。

note.cn: rubbish 是垃圾，rubble 则是碎砖石。

entries.definition: broken stones from a building
entries.definitionCN: 碎石；瓦砾

entries.definition: to move a hand over a surface
entries.definitionCN: 摩擦；擦

entries.definition: a soft material from tree sap
entries.definitionCN: 橡胶

entries.definition: waste from homes

entries.definition: things thrown away
entries.definitionCN: 废物；垃圾

entries.definition: material that is not used

normalIntro.en: Rubbish is what is thrown out or has no worth.
normalIntro.cn: rubbish 是被扔掉或没有价值的东西。

normal.en: The street was covered in rubbish after the fair.

examples.en: The film was dismissed as rubbish by critics.

examples.en: He talks rubbish when he is nervous.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rubbish」读起来像「垃圾堆里拉比什」，可以联想一袋被人丢弃的垃圾。

root: 中古英语 robous（碎石、废料）进入英语后扩展为「垃圾、废物、废话」。

sensesIntro.en: Rubbish means waste material, things of poor quality, or foolish talk.
sensesIntro.cn: rubbish 意为废弃物、劣质东西，或废话。

branches.en: The base sense is physical waste.

branches.en: Waste becomes a judgment of quality.

branches.en: Worthless things become worthless words.

definition_zh: 阻止；防止；使无法；妨碍；预防
definition_en: to stop something from happening, or to make it impossible for someone to do something
core_image: 有人还没走到门口，一条手臂已经横在门框上把路挡住
scene: 雨天路滑，小区门口新铺了一道减速带，旁边立着一块提示牌。 The speed bump was installed to prevent accidents at the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 prevent 是「预防、防止发生」（第 3 个义项：采取措施，使事故一类的事不发生）；句意为这道减速带是为了防止门口发生事故而设。图中可辨识景物：减速带、雨后的路面、提示牌。

pos.zh: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍

derivatives.zh: 由 prevent 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「阻止；预防」
由 prevent 加 -ive 构成，义为「预防的；防护的」
由 prevent 加 -able 构成，义为「可预防的；可以避免的」

senses.title: To stop an event from taking place
senses.definition: to stop an event or action before it can happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事件或行动来不及发生
senses.example: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
senses.exampleCN: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。
senses.why: Latin praevenire meant to come before someone; arriving at a place first is what lets you stand in the way of what follows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevenire 意为「先于某人到来」，先一步赶到某处，才有机会挡在后头那件事的前面，所以「阻止」是「先来」的直接结果。

senses.title: To make it impossible for someone to act
senses.titleCN: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍
senses.definition: to make it impossible for someone to do what they intended
senses.definitionCN: 使某人无法做成原本打算做的事
senses.example: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。
senses.why: Here no force is aimed at the person; the word only reports that an obstacle got there first and the action never began.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不对某人施加力量，只是说明障碍先到了，那个动作始终没能开始，所以介词 from 后面接的是被挡住的行动。

senses.title: To reduce the risk of illness or damage
senses.definition: to take action so that illness, damage, or trouble does not develop
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施，使疾病、损害或麻烦不致发展起来
senses.example: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。
senses.why: Medicine widened the focus from one event to a whole class of risk: acting early becomes a habit rather than a single block in a doorway.
senses.whyCN: 医学把焦点从单一事件扩大成一整类风险：提前动手变成习惯，而不再是门口一次性的拦阻，于是「预防」从「阻止」里独立出来。

senses.title: To go before, in older religious language
senses.definition: to go before or act ahead of someone, a sense kept mainly in old prayers
senses.definitionCN: 走在某人之前或先行行动，这一义项主要保留在古老祷词中
senses.example: The old prayer asks God to prevent us in all our doings.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老祷词祈求上帝在我们一切所行的事上先行引导。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin meaning surviving in English; modern usage narrowed the word, but the prayer book never changed.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义在英语里的遗留：字面上就是「走在前面」。现代用法把词义收窄了，祷词却一直没改，所以这个古老义项仍能读到。

intro.en: Prevent is built from a Latin prefix meaning before and the verb to come: to prevent is, quite literally, to get there first, and hindering grew out of that head start.
intro.cn: prevent 由表示「在前」的拉丁前缀与动词「来」构成：字面上就是「先到一步」；阻挡的义项，正是从这个抢先到达的动作长出来的。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, the same prefix that appears in predict and prepare.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，predict 与 prepare 也用了这个前缀。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it supplies the ven- seen in intervene, convene and event.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，intervene、convene、event 里的 ven- 都来自它。

items.en: Praevenire meant to come before someone, to arrive ahead of them, and so to anticipate or forestall.
items.cn: praevenire 意为「先于某人来到」，即赶在对方前头到达，因此引申为预先、抢先拦下。

items.en: Old French prevenir kept both the sense of arriving first and the sense of hindering by getting there early.
items.cn: 古法语 prevenir 同时保留「先到」与「因先到而阻挡」两层意思。

items.en: Modern English dropped the literal meaning and kept the result: something is prevented when it never gets to happen.
items.cn: 现代英语丢掉了字面上的「先到」，只留下结果：一件事始终没能发生，就是被 prevent 了。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for coming; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for blocking, avoiding and putting off harm.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「来」的动词展开；近义组收阻挡、避开与消解祸患的动词。

entries.definition: The act of stopping something before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前将其阻止的行为；预防。

entries.definition: Intended to stop illness or trouble before it starts.
entries.definitionCN: 意在疾病或麻烦开始前就加以阻止的；预防性的。

entries.definition: Able to be stopped before it happens.
entries.definitionCN: 可以在发生前被阻止的；可预防的。

entries.definition: Coming before or anticipating something; used mainly in theology.
entries.definitionCN: 先于某事先行而来的；主要用于神学语境。

entries.definition: To keep away from something so that it does not happen to you.
entries.definitionCN: 远远避开某物，使它不落到自己身上。

entries.definition: To make progress or action difficult.
entries.definitionCN: 使进展或行动变得困难。

entries.definition: To turn something bad away before it arrives.
entries.definitionCN: 在坏事到来之前把它挡开。

entries.definition: To make someone decide not to act, usually through fear of the consequences.
entries.definitionCN: 使人因后果的威慑而决定不做某事。

entries.definition: To end an action that has already started.
entries.definitionCN: 使已经开始的动作停止。

normalIntro.en: The word puts a Latin prefix meaning before onto the verb to come, and its family keeps the picture of arriving first.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在表示「来」的拉丁动词前加上「在前」的前缀，同族词都保留着「先一步到达」的画面。

normal.en: Prae- plus venire: prevent is to come before, and only later to block because you got there first.
normal.cn: prae- 加 venire：prevent 本是「先来」，后来才因先到而挡住。

normal.en: The ven- of prevent means come, as in invent and convene; pretend has a different verb, tendere, meaning stretch, so the two share only the prefix.
normal.cn: prevent 里的 ven- 意为「来」，invent、convene 同此；pretend 用的是另一个动词 tendere（伸展），两词只共享前缀，词源并不相同。

normal.en: Prevention is the noun and preventive the adjective; both name stopping something ahead of time.
normal.cn: prevention 是名词，preventive 是形容词，两者都指提前挡住。

normal.en: Preventable marks what can be stopped, with the same -able heard in avoidable and curable.
normal.cn: preventable 标注「拦得住的」，后缀 -able 与 avoidable、curable 里的相同。

normal.en: The pattern「prevent somebody from doing something」keeps the image of a body standing in another person's way.
normal.cn: 搭配「prevent somebody from doing something」保留了「一个人挡在另一个人路上」的画面。

abstract.en: To prevent is to win a race nobody watches: the best prevention leaves nothing to see afterwards.
abstract.cn: prevent 是赢下一场没人观看的比赛：最好的预防，事后什么也看不见。

abstract.en: The word once meant arrive first, and every act of prevention is still a small race against an event.
abstract.cn: 这个词原本只表示「先到」，而每一次预防，仍是在和某个事件抢时间。

abstract.en: Prevent and pretend share a prefix but not a road: one comes first, the other stretches a screen.
abstract.cn: prevent 与 pretend 共享前缀，却不同路：一个抢先赶到，一个撑起帘子。

examples.en: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
examples.cn: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。

examples.en: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
examples.cn: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。

examples.en: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
examples.cn: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「扑来问」——人还没进门就先扑上去问一句，顺势把人拦在门外。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ venire（来）构成 praevenire，本义「先来、抢先到达」，引申为「预先阻挡」，经古法语 prevenir 进入英语。ve-nire 是「来」，与 pretend 所用的 tendere（伸展）不同源，两词只共享前缀 prae-。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arriving before something else; the senses run from stopping an event, to blocking a person, to forestalling illness, and finally to the old literal sense of going before.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「赶在某事之前到达」；义项从阻止事件，到挡住某人，到防病于未然，最后回到古老的「先行」本义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm raised across a doorway a moment before someone reaches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人还没走到门口，一条手臂已经横在那里。

branches.en: a hand shutting the window before the rain starts
branches.cn: 雨还没下，一只手先把窗关上

branches.en: a guard standing in a doorway with arms spread
branches.cn: 守卫张开手臂站在门口

branches.en: a needle given before the season of flu
branches.cn: 流感季节来临前打的一针

branches.en: an old prayer asking to be led from the front
branches.cn: 古老祷词求人先行引领

branches.en: a speed bump slowing every car at the gate
branches.cn: 减速带让门口每辆车都慢下来

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix of place to a Latin verb of coming, then adds English endings that name the act, the quality and the possibility.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示位置的拉丁前缀与表示「来」的拉丁动词结合，再加上命名行为、性质与可能性的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

core_image: 被放在讨论中央、供人观看与研究的那个东西
scene: 今天这节课的主题是天气。 The subject of today's lesson is the weather.
sceneCN: 这里 subject 是「主题」（第 1 个义项）；句意：今天这节课的主题是天气。

征服；服从

senses.title: Topic
senses.definition: the thing being discussed or written about
senses.definitionCN: 正在被讨论或书写的事物
senses.example: The subject of today's lesson is the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 今天这节课的主题是天气。
senses.why: This is the basic topic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的主题义项。

senses.title: Course of study
senses.definition: an area of knowledge studied at school
senses.definitionCN: 在学校学习的一个知识领域
senses.example: History is her favourite subject.

senses.why: A topic of study becomes a school subject.
senses.whyCN: 被研究的主题成了学校科目。

senses.title: Person studied
senses.definition: a person or thing used in a test or study
senses.definitionCN: 用于测试或研究的人或物
senses.example: The subjects were asked to sleep well.
senses.exampleCN: 受试者被要求好好睡觉。
senses.why: Research places people under study.
senses.whyCN: 研究把人置于被观察的位置。

senses.title: Affected by

senses.definitionCN: 容易受到某事影响的

senses.why: Being under control becomes being open to change.
senses.whyCN: 处于控制之下，引申为易受变动影响。

items.cn: subiectus 意为置于权力之下。

normalIntro.cn: subject 是课程、研究或统治者置于关注之下的东西。

normal.en: History is her favourite subject.

abstract.en: Every subject is a world someone chose to look at.

abstract.en: To be subject to time is to be human.

abstract.en: The subject of a life is rarely written down.

examples.en: The subject of today's lesson is the weather.

intro.cn: subject 借助 -ive 和 -ion 构成形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base iect- meant thrown.

definition_zh: 雨；雨水；下雨；如雨般落下
definition_en: water that falls from clouds in drops; to fall as rain; a large number of things falling or arriving at once
core_image: 屋檐下连成一线落下的水珠
scene: 早晨的街道上，行人撑起伞，水沿着屋檐一线线落下。 The rain kept the whole village indoors for two days.
sceneCN: 这里 rain 是「雨」（第 1 个义项：从云中落下的水滴）；句意为这场雨让整个村子两天都待在室内。画面里可留意：伞面、屋檐滴落的水线、空荡的街道。

derivatives.zh: rain 加 -y，指多雨的、下雨的
rain 与 fall 复合，指一段时间内的降雨量
rain 与 coat 复合，指防雨的外套

senses.title: Water falling from clouds
senses.definition: water that falls from clouds in drops and reaches the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从云中以水滴形式落下并到达地面的水
senses.example: The rain lasted all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨下了一整个上午。
senses.why: Old English regn named the falling water directly, and the word has stayed close to the weather ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 regn 直接命名这种落下的水，此后这个词一直紧贴天气这一含义。

senses.title: To fall as rain
senses.definition: to fall from the sky as drops of water, used of the weather itself
senses.definitionCN: 以水滴形式从天空落下，用于描述天气本身
senses.example: It rained for three days without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 雨连下了三天没停。
senses.why: The noun became an impersonal verb, so English can say it rains without naming who or what is acting.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了无人称动词，因此英语可以说 it rains，而不必指出动作的执行者。

senses.title: A great number falling at once
senses.definition: a large number of things coming down or arriving together, as if falling like drops
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物像水滴一样同时落下或到来
senses.example: A rain of stones fell from the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵石块从崖上落下。
senses.why: Because rain is countless drops arriving together, the word became a picture for anything that comes in a shower.
senses.whyCN: 雨是无数水滴一同到来，因此这个词成了任何「成阵而至」之物的画面。

intro.en: Rain is a native English word from Old English regn, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: rain 是英语本族词，来自古英语 regn，在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Regn meant rain, and it was used in compounds for storms and wet weather.
items.cn: regn 意为雨，也用于构成表示风暴与潮湿天气的复合词。

items.en: The word is reconstructed in older Germanic with the same sense, and related forms appear across northern Europe.
items.cn: 这个词在更早的日耳曼语中被重构为同样的意思，相关形式遍布北欧。

items.en: Middle English rain kept the spelling close to the old form while the verb rained developed beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 rain 拼写接近古形，同时发展出动词 rained。

items.en: Rain combined with fall and coat to name what rain does and what protects against it.
items.cn: rain 与 fall、coat 组合，命名雨的作用以及防雨之物。

items.en: Modern English uses rain for the water, the weather, and figuratively for anything arriving in quantity.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rain 指水、天气，并比喻任何大量到来之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and one homophone; the near-meaning group gathers words for falling water.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与一个同音词；近义组收表示落水的词。

entries.definition: Having a lot of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 多雨的。

entries.definition: The amount of rain that falls in a period.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内的降雨量。

entries.definition: A coat that keeps rain out.
entries.definitionCN: 防雨的外套。

entries.definition: The period during which a monarch rules, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 君主统治的时期，同音但不同源。

entries.definition: A short fall of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 一阵短促的降雨。

entries.definition: A very heavy fall of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 极猛烈的降雨。

entries.definition: Light rain falling in fine drops.
entries.definitionCN: 以细小雨滴落下的毛毛雨。

entries.definition: Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow or hail.
entries.definitionCN: 以雨、雪或冰雹形式从云中落下的水。

normalIntro.en: The word names the falling water, then the weather, then anything that arrives like drops in a shower.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词先命名落下的水，再指天气，最后指任何像水滴一样成阵而至的东西。

normal.en: Rain and reign sound the same, but one falls from the sky while the other is held by a monarch.
normal.cn: rain 与 reign 同音，但一个从天上落下，一个由君主掌握。

normal.en: Rainy is the adjective, rainfall is the measured amount, and raincoat is the thing you wear.
normal.cn: rainy 是形容词，rainfall 是测得的雨量，raincoat 是穿在身上的东西。

normal.en: It rained is impersonal: the it does not point to anyone, because weather has no actor.
normal.cn: it rained 是无人称句：it 不指向任何人，因为天气没有执行者。

normal.en: Rain or shine is the phrase for doing something whatever the weather.
normal.cn: rain or shine 是无论天气如何都要做某事的说法。

normal.en: A rain of stones uses the weather word for anything falling in great numbers.
normal.cn: a rain of stones 用天气词指大量落下的任何东西。

abstract.en: Rain is the most ordinary proof that something can arrive without being invited.
abstract.cn: 雨是「事物会不请自来」这件事最平常的证明。

abstract.en: Farmers read rain as promise or threat, which shows how one word can carry both hope and fear.
abstract.cn: 农民把雨读成许诺或威胁，可见同一个词能同时承载希望与恐惧。

abstract.en: A rain of stones and a rain of questions share the word because both overwhelm by number.
abstract.cn: 石雨与问题雨共用一个词，因为两者都以数量压倒了人。

examples.en: The rain stopped just before the match began.
examples.cn: 比赛开始前雨刚好停了。

examples.en: It rained so hard that the road disappeared under water.
examples.cn: 雨下得太大，路面被水淹没了。

examples.en: A rain of small stones rattled on the roof.
examples.cn: 一阵小石块噼里啪啦打在屋顶上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞恩」——天上落下的水滴一颗颗，记住 rain 是雨、下雨。

root: 古英语 regn（雨）→ 中古英语 rain → 现代英语 rain；同族有 rainy、rainfall、raincoat。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is falling water; the senses divide into the water itself, the weather, and anything arriving in a shower.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落下的水」；义项分为水本身、天气，以及任何成阵而至之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: drops falling in a continuous line from the edge of a roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：水珠从屋檐边连成一线落下。

branches.en: an empty street under umbrellas
branches.cn: 伞下空荡的街道

branches.en: a window grey with weather
branches.cn: 被天气染灰的窗

branches.en: stones rattling down a cliff
branches.cn: 从崖上滚落的石块

branches.en: the same falling, once as water and once as stones
branches.cn: 同一种下落，一次是水，一次是石头

branches.en: weather that arrives and things that arrive in numbers
branches.cn: 到来的天气与成批到来的东西

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built from English compounds and a simple adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是本族短词，其词族由英语复合词与一个简单的形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 聪明的；智能的；有才智的
definition_en: able to learn, think and understand well; showing good judgment
core_image: 灯泡在头顶亮起的瞬间
scene: 小狗会自己开门闩了。 An intelligent robot vacuum maps the room.
sceneCN: 这里 intelligent 是「智能的」（第 2 个义项：机器具备理解能力）；句意：智能扫地机器人会绘制房间地图。

derivatives.zh: intelligent 加名词后缀，义为「智力；情报」
intelligent 加副词后缀，义为「聪明地」
同源名词，义为「知识分子阶层」

senses.title: Quick to learn and think
senses.definition: good at learning, thinking and understanding
senses.definitionCN: 善于学习、思考与理解
senses.example: She is an intelligent student who asks sharp questions.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个聪明的学生，提问犀利。
senses.why: The bulb lights before others do.
senses.whyCN: 灯泡比别人家的先亮。

senses.title: Showing smart design in machines
senses.definition: able to gather data and act sensibly, of devices
senses.definitionCN: 指设备能采集数据并合理行动
senses.example: Intelligent traffic lights reduce jams.
senses.exampleCN: 智能红绿灯减少拥堵。
senses.why: The bulb switches itself on when needed.
senses.whyCN: 灯泡会在需要时自动亮起。

senses.title: Wise in choice
senses.definition: showing good judgment in choices
senses.definitionCN: 在选择上表现出良好的判断力
senses.example: It was an intelligent decision to wait.
senses.exampleCN: 等待是明智的决定。
senses.why: The bulb stays dark when light would hurt.
senses.whyCN: 该暗时灯泡保持熄灭。

senses.title: Sly in a clever way
senses.definition: clever in a quick-witted, sometimes cunning way
senses.definitionCN: 机敏而略带狡黠的聪明
senses.example: An intelligent thief leaves no trace.
senses.exampleCN: 机敏的窃贼不留痕迹。
senses.why: The bulb winks before anyone notices.
senses.whyCN: 灯泡在无人注意时眨了眨。

intro.en: Intelligent comes from Latin intelligere, to choose between or understand, from inter- (between) and legere (to pick, to read). Mind as a picker of the right option.
intro.cn: intelligent 来自拉丁语 intelligere「在……之间挑选、理解」，由 inter-「之间」+ legere「挑选、阅读」构成；心智即挑选正确选项的读者。

items.en: Latin legere meant to pick out, to read; it gave elect, select and lecture.
items.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为拣选、阅读；同根词有 elect、select、lecture。

items.en: inter- plus legere formed intelligere: to pick between, discern.
items.cn: inter- 加 legere 构成 intelligere：在两者间拣选、辨识。

items.en: intelligens named one who discerns well.
items.cn: intelligens 指善于辨识之人。

items.en: Old French lent the spelling the nt ending we still write.
items.cn: 古法语借来了我们沿用至今的 nt 结尾。

items.en: Middle English inteligent meant understanding.
items.cn: 中古英语 inteligent 意为善解。

items.en: Modern English applied it to people, choices and finally machines.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于人、选择，最终用于机器。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the pick-root family. The meaning group compares words of bright minds.
note.cn: 形近组收录「拣选」词根词族；词义组比较头脑聪明的词。

entries.definition: the noun: mind power or secret reports.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：智力或情报。

entries.definition: in a smart way.
entries.definitionCN: 聪明地。

entries.definition: able to be understood.
entries.definitionCN: 可理解的。

entries.definition: quick at learning or tricks.
entries.definitionCN: 学得快或点子多。

entries.definition: informal bright; also stylish.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中的机灵；也指潇洒。

entries.definition: showing long-view judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 有长远判断的智慧。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picking root, the lightbulb image and the machine twist.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「拣选」词根、灯泡意象与机器转折。

normal.en: inter- plus legere: the mind picks the right option.
normal.cn: inter- 加 legere：心智拣出对的选项。

normal.en: elect and select share the picking root.
normal.cn: elect 与 select 共享拣选词根。

normal.en: intelligence is the noun twin, also spy reports.
normal.cn: intelligence 是名词孪生词，也指情报。

normal.en: an intelligent vacuum maps your room.
normal.cn: 智能吸尘器会画房间地图。

normal.en: intelligible means easy to understand.
normal.cn: intelligible 意为易懂的。

abstract.en: One image: a bulb that lights before the question ends.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：问题未完灯泡已亮。

abstract.en: To be intelligent is to read between the options.
abstract.cn: intelligent 就是在选项之间读出答案。

abstract.en: The lamp knows when to shine and when to rest.
abstract.cn: 这盏灯知道何时亮、何时歇。

examples.en: He gave an intelligent reply to a hard question.
examples.cn: 他对难题给出了聪明的回答。

examples.en: Dolphins are highly intelligent animals.
examples.cn: 海豚是非常聪明的动物。

examples.en: Invest your savings intelligently.
examples.cn: 要聪明地投资你的积蓄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因太利真特」：因脑子太利落，答案特别真， intelligent。

root: 拉丁语 inter-「之间」+ legere「拣选、阅读」→ intelligere「辨识、理解」→ intelligens「善辨识者」→ 古法语 → 中古英语 inteligent → 现代英语 intelligent；同根词 select、elect、lecture。

sensesIntro.en: Intelligent is the early bulb: a mind that picks fast, a machine that switches itself, a choice that waits wisely, and a wink of cunning.
sensesIntro.cn: intelligent 是先亮的灯泡：快速拣选的头脑、会自己开关的机器、懂得等待的明智，以及狡黠的一眨。

core.en: A bulb that lights before others, knowing when to shine and when to stay dark.
core.cn: 比别人先亮的灯泡，知道何时发光、何时熄灭。

branches.en: MIND: an intelligent student asks sharp questions.
branches.cn: 头脑：聪明学生提问犀利。

branches.en: MACHINE: intelligent traffic lights reduce jams.
branches.cn: 机器：智能红绿灯减拥堵。

branches.en: JUDGMENT: it was intelligent to wait.
branches.cn: 判断：等待是明智的。

branches.en: CLEVERNESS: an intelligent thief leaves no trace.
branches.cn: 机敏：机敏的贼不留痕。

branches.en: PICKING: choosing well between options.
branches.cn: 拣选：在选项间择优。

intro.en: Intelligent builds intelligence, intelligently and intelligible.
intro.cn: intelligent 构成 intelligence、intelligently、intelligible。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the picking verb legere behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的拣选动词 legere。

definition_zh: 物质；事情；问题；要紧、有关系；【医】脓液
definition_en: the physical stuff that things are made of, an affair under discussion, or to be important
core_image: 一块被雨水泡软的黑泥，手指一捏就能变形，也能弄脏任何碰到它的东西
scene: 泥地刚被雨水浸透，脚一踩就陷下去，鞋底带起黏稠的一团。 The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 matter 指构成物体的有形之物（第 1 个义项：与形式相对、可被感官触及的实体材料）；句意：那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。图中可辨识物件：泥洼、沾泥的靴子、铁锹、水桶；对应第 1 个义项。

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 就事论事的；不动声色的（由本词与「事实」一词构成的复合形容词）
反物质（加表示「相反」的前缀构成，指电荷相反的物质）
无实质内容的（加表示「没有」的后缀构成）
含脓的（加形容词后缀构成，旧医学用法，现已罕用）

senses.title: Physical substance
senses.definition: the physical substance that occupies space and can be seen or touched
senses.definitionCN: 占据空间、可被看见或摸到的实体材料
senses.example: The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。
senses.why: matter goes back to Latin materia, which meant timber and the stuff a thing is built from, so the physical sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: matter 上溯到拉丁 materia，本指木料与造物所用的料，因此「有形之物」是最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: An affair or business
senses.titleCN: 一件待办或已办的事情
senses.definition: a situation, event or piece of business that someone deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某人需要处理的情境、事件或事务
senses.example: She settled a few private matters before leaving for the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边之前，她先处理了几件私事。
senses.why: Latin materia also named the subject under discussion, so the stuff of a talk became the affair itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 materia 也指谈论的题目，于是「谈话的料」就变成了「事情本身」。

senses.title: A problem to be solved
senses.titleCN: 出了差错、需要弄清的问题
senses.definition: a trouble or difficulty, especially one whose cause is not yet known
senses.definitionCN: 麻烦或困难，尤指原因尚未查明的那一种
senses.example: The mechanic asked what the matter was with the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工问发动机出了什么毛病。
senses.why: an affair that has gone wrong is still an affair, so the same word shifted from business to trouble.
senses.whyCN: 出了岔子的事情仍然是一件事情，这个词便从「事务」滑到「麻烦」。

senses.title: To be important
senses.definition: to be of importance or consequence to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事具有重要性或后果
senses.example: Accuracy matters more than speed in this laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间实验室里，准确比速度更要紧。
senses.why: what has substance has weight, and English turned that picture into the verb sense of counting for something.
senses.whyCN: 有实体就有分量，英语把这个画面变成了「算得上数」的动词义。

senses.title: The topic of a text or talk
senses.definition: the subject or content that a piece of writing, speech or study is about
senses.definitionCN: 一篇文章、一段讲话或一项研究所谈论的主题与内容
senses.example: The matter of the lecture was soil chemistry in dry regions.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座的主题是干旱地区的土壤化学。
senses.why: the material of a text is what it carries, and that carrying sense became the topic it treats.
senses.whyCN: 文章的「料」就是它所承载的东西，这一承载义再转为它所处理的主题。

senses.title: Grounds for concern
senses.titleCN: 值得忧虑或申诉的根据
senses.definition: a reason or grounds for a feeling, claim or action
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪、主张或行动的根据与理由
senses.example: The inspectors found matter for concern in the water samples.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员在采水样中发现了值得忧虑的情况。
senses.why: a matter is something that exists and can be pointed at, so it came to mean a fact solid enough to base a claim on.
senses.whyCN: 事情是存在且指得出的事物，于是引申为「站得住脚、可作依据的事实」。

senses.title: Pus from a wound
senses.definition: the fluid that forms in an infected wound, formerly called matter
senses.definitionCN: 感染伤口中生成的液体，旧时称作 matter
senses.example: The old surgical notes describe the wound discharging matter.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手术记录描述伤口流出脓液。
senses.why: early medicine used matter for any fluid substance of the body, and pus was simply the matter a wound produced.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学用 matter 泛指体内各种液体，脓不过是伤口生成的「物质」。

senses.title: Content as opposed to form
senses.titleCN: 与形式相对的实质内容
senses.definition: the substantive content of a work, as distinct from its style or outward form
senses.definitionCN: 作品的实际内容，与风格或外在形式相对
senses.example: The matter of the essay outweighs its elegant phrasing.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇随笔的内容比它漂亮的措辞更有分量。
senses.why: philosophy opposed matter to form, and literary criticism then asked whether a work had matter behind its shape.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把「质料」与「形式」对举，文学批评随后追问一部作品在形之外有没有实质。

intro.en: Matter came into English through Old French from Latin materia 'timber, stuff, subject'. The common claim that materia derives from mater 'mother' is a hypothesis, not a settled derivation.
intro.cn: matter 经古法语来自拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」。常有人说 materia 由 mater「母亲」派生，那是假说，并非已定的词源。

items.en: Materia meant timber and the material a thing is made from, and by extension the subject of a discussion.
items.cn: materia 指木料以及造物所用的材料，引申为谈论的题目。

items.en: A widely repeated suggestion links materia to mater 'mother', as if the stuff were the mother of the object; this remains a hypothesis and is not established.
items.cn: 一种广为流传的说法把 materia 与 mater「母亲」联系起来，仿佛材料是器物的母亲；这仍属假说，未获证实。

items.en: Old French matere carried both the physical sense and the sense of a subject or affair into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 matere 在诺曼时期之后把「物质」与「题目、事务」两义一并带入英语。

items.en: Middle English matter already covered stuff, a business, a question and grounds for complaint, so the wide sense range is old, not modern.
items.cn: 中古英语的 matter 已兼指物质、事务、问题与申诉的理由，可见义域之宽古已有之，并非现代才有。

items.en: Medical writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries used matter for bodily fluid and especially for pus, a use that has since narrowed.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的医学文献用 matter 指体液，尤指脓，这一用法后来收窄。

items.en: The first recorded dates for several senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 若干义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十三世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group contains forms that look or sound close to matter but may sit on a different root; the second group contains words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音与 matter 接近、但未必同源的词；第二组是与之部分同义的词。

entries.definition: Built on Latin materialis from materia, so it is the adjective and noun grown from the same stock as matter, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 materialis 构成，而 materialis 出自 materia，因此它是与 matter 同出一源的名词与形容词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A French-shaped doublet of material, borrowed later for military equipment and supplies; it shares the Latin source but not the everyday meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 是 material 的法语式借形词，后借入指军用装备与物资；与 material 同源，但日常义不同。

entries.definition: From Latin mater 'mother' through maternellus; it is related to mater, and only through the unproven mater-materia hypothesis could it be called a cousin of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 经 maternellus 出自拉丁 mater「母亲」；它与 mater 有关，只有借助尚未证实的「母亲—材料」假说，才能算作 matter 的远亲。

entries.definition: From Latin matrix 'womb, mould', built on mater; it names a mould or grid, and does not descend from materia.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 matrix「子宫、模具」，由 mater 构成；它指模具或网格，并非由 materia 传下。

entries.definition: Physical stuff considered as what stands under qualities; matter stresses the material, substance stresses independent existence.
entries.definitionCN: 把物质看作承载属性的基底；matter 强调材料，substance 强调独立存在。

entries.definition: A matter of business or public concern; it covers only the affair sense and never the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 指事务或公众关注之事；只覆盖「事务」义，绝不指物质。

entries.definition: A topic on which people disagree; it is narrower than matter because it always implies debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们有分歧的议题；比 matter 窄，因为它总含争辩之意。

entries.definition: The everyday word for unspecified material; matter is its neutral and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指未指明材料的日常说法；matter 是它中性、技术化的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin materia first meant timber, so matter is the stuff a thing is built from.
normal.cn: 拉丁 materia 最初指木料，因此 matter 就是造物所用的料。

normal.en: The family runs matter, material, materially, immaterial and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 matter、material、materially、immaterial 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the affair sense: a matter of time, as a matter of fact, no matter what.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「事情」义：只是时间问题、事实上、无论发生什么。

normal.en: Subject matter keeps the topic sense visible in publishing and teaching.
normal.cn: 「主题素材」这一说法让「主题」义在出版与教学里一直可见。

normal.en: The verb is used in questions of value: it matters, it does not matter.
normal.cn: 动词义出现在价值判断里：这要紧、这不要紧。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay that takes the shape of whatever presses into it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土，什么按上去就留下什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with one folded note on it, and everyone asks about that note first.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上只有一张折起的字条，所有人先问的都是那张字条。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the pan with real goods sinks and the empty pan rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，装了实物的那端沉下去，空的那端翘起来。

examples.en: In legal drafting, the matter of a contract means its operative content rather than its layout.
examples.cn: 在法律起草中，合同的 matter 指其有效内容，而不是排版。

examples.en: Dark matter does not emit light, yet its gravity holds galaxies together.
examples.cn: 暗物质不发光，但它的引力把星系维系在一起。

examples.en: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as the measurements stay exact.
examples.cn: 只要测量保持精确，你走得多慢都不要紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈特」——妈妈特别在意的那件事，就是要紧的事 → 事情、要紧；妈妈捏的那团泥，就是物质

root: 拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」（一说由 mater「母亲」派生，仅为常见假说）→ 古法语 matere「材料、事务」→ 英语 matter；「问题」与「脓」义由「事情」「体内物质」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one lump of stuff: it is the material of things, then the material of talk, then the affair, the trouble inside it, the fact that carries weight, the topic of a text, the fluid in a wound, and finally content set against form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一团「料」辐射出去：先是造物的材料，再是谈话的材料，继而成为事情、事情里的麻烦、有分量的事实、文本的主题、伤口的液体，最后是与形式相对的实质内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet clay that can be shaped, weighed and pointed at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团湿黏土，可被塑形、称重、指认。

branches.en: THE LUMP ITSELF: clay in the yard and pus in a wound are both stuff a body or a boot meets.
branches.cn: 这团东西本身：院里的泥与伤口的脓，都是身体或靴子会碰到的实体。

branches.en: THE AFFAIR AND ITS SNAG: business first, then the trouble discovered inside it.
branches.cn: 事情与其中的疙瘩：先是事务，再是事务里查出的麻烦。

branches.en: WEIGHT THAT COUNTS: what has substance can tip a decision, so matter becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 有分量才算数：有实体就能压动决定，于是 matter 变成动词。

branches.en: STUFF POINTED AT: the material of a text turns into its topic, and a solid fact into grounds.
branches.cn: 被指认的料：文本的材料变成主题，扎实的事实变成依据。

branches.en: CONTENT AGAINST FORM: philosophy keeps the lump as what remains when style is stripped away.
branches.cn: 内容对形式：哲学把那团料保留为剥去风格后剩下的东西。

intro.en: Matter is built on a Latin root that also yields material and immaterial, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: matter 建立在一个拉丁词根上，同一词根还生出 material 与 immaterial，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia supplies matter, material and materialis; mater supplies maternal and matrix, with the materia link remaining a hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material 一系；mater 衍生 maternal 与 matrix 一系，而 materia 与 mater 的联系仍属假说。

items.example: The root gives the picture of stuff a thing is built from.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「造物所用之料」的画面。

items.example: Its link to materia is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.exampleCN: 它与 materia 的联系只是假说，并非已证的派生。

items.example: The adjective suffix turns stuff into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀把「料」变成描述性的词。

items.example: Material keeps both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: It also shapes editorial and commercial.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The negation covers both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: The plan materialized as a real building.
items.exampleCN: 计划落实成了一座真实的建筑。

items.example: The later borrowing narrowed to army supplies.
items.exampleCN: 后借入的这一形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 邮政；邮件；职位；柱子；邮寄；张贴；发布
definition_en: the mail service or the mail itself; a job; an upright pole; to send by mail or to put a message where people can see it
core_image: 一根木桩立在路边，桩上钉着一块写满消息的木板
scene: 村口的老木门上贴着一张寻物启事，路过的人都停下脚步看。 Someone had posted a notice about a lost dog on the gate.
sceneCN: 这里是「张贴、发布」（第 5 个义项：把消息公开出来）；句意为有人在门上贴了一张寻狗启事。画面里可留意木桩、旧门和那张被风掀起的纸。

derivatives.zh: post 加表示费用的后缀 -age 构成，指「邮费」
post 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，表示「邮政的」
post（张贴）加 -er 构成，原指张贴的告示，现多指「海报」

senses.title: The mail service and the letters it carries
senses.definition: the system that collects and delivers letters and parcels, or those letters and parcels themselves
senses.definitionCN: 收寄并投递信件、包裹的系统，也指这些信件与包裹本身
senses.example: The cheque came by post this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 支票是今天上午邮寄到的。
senses.why: Post first named a relay station where horses were changed; the letters that travelled from station to station took the name, and then the whole service did.
senses.whyCN: post 最初指换马的驿站；一站一站传下去的信件借用了这个名称，最后整套邮政系统也沿用了它。

senses.title: A job or position in an organization
senses.definition: a job in an organization, especially one with a title and fixed duties
senses.definitionCN: 组织中的一个职位，尤指有头衔、职责固定者
senses.example: She applied for a post in the finance department.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了财务部的一个职位。
senses.why: A post was also a place where a soldier or official was stationed, so the word slid from the spot to the duty held at that spot.
senses.whyCN: post 也指士兵或官员驻扎的地点，词义便从「那个位置」滑到「在那个位置上承担的职务」。

senses.title: An upright pole set in the ground
senses.definition: a strong upright piece of wood or metal fixed in the ground, used to support something or mark a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 固定在地里的坚固木柱或金属柱，用来支撑物件或标示界线
senses.example: A wooden post marks the end of the path.
senses.exampleCN: 一根木桩标出了小路的尽头。
senses.why: This is the oldest line of all: Latin postis named a doorpost or upright beam, and English kept the solid object.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一条线：拉丁语 postis 指门柱或直立的梁木，英语保留了这件实物本身。

senses.title: To send a letter or parcel by mail
senses.definition: to send a letter, parcel or message through the postal system
senses.definitionCN: 通过邮政系统寄出信件、包裹或消息
senses.example: I posted the documents to the embassy yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 我昨天把文件寄给了大使馆。
senses.why: Once post named the mail service, the noun turned into a verb: to post something is to hand it over to that service.
senses.whyCN: post 既然指邮政系统，名词就顺势转为动词，表示「把东西交给这套系统」。

senses.title: To put a notice or message where people can see it
senses.definition: to put up a notice in public, or to publish a message, picture or piece of writing online
senses.definitionCN: 把通知张贴在公共处，或在网上发布消息、图片、文字
senses.example: The school posted the exam results on its website.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把考试成绩发布在网站上。
senses.why: A post is a fixed place; to post something was to fix it there for everyone to read, and the internet reused the same picture for a screen.
senses.whyCN: post 是一个固定的位置；把东西 post 出来就是把它固定在那里让人人可读，网络时代把这幅画面搬到了屏幕上。

intro.en: Two Latin lines meet in this short word: postis, an upright beam, and posta, a station on a road, which itself comes from ponere, to place.
intro.cn: 两条拉丁线索在这个短词里汇合：postis 是直立的梁柱，posta 是路上的驿站，而 posta 又出自 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Postis meant a doorpost or upright beam, and this line alone gives English the wooden pole.
items.cn: postis 意为门柱或直立的梁木，仅这一条线就给了英语「木柱」这个义项。

items.en: The mail line starts elsewhere: ponere meant to put or place, and its participle positus, placed, stands behind the later station word.
items.cn: 邮政那条线另有起点：ponere 意为放置，它的过去分词 positus（被放置的）是后来「驿站」一词的背后形式。

items.en: Posta named a station on a road where horses and messengers were changed, a place where things were set down.
items.cn: posta 指路上换马、换信使的站点，也就是把人和物「安置下来」的地方。

items.en: English borrowed the French form poste for the riders and the letters, so post came to mean the mail and the office that handled it.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 poste，指骑马送信的人和信件，于是 post 兼指邮件与经办邮件的机构。

items.en: Modern English keeps both lines apart: the beam stays a post, while the station line grows into job posts, posting a letter and posting online.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条线分开保留：梁柱仍是 post，而「驿站」一线则长出职位、寄信与网络发布。

note.en: The first group collects words built on post with different endings; the second collects words for mail, for jobs and for poles, the three fields this word covers.
note.cn: 形近组收在 post 上加不同词尾构成的词；近义组收邮件、职位、柱子这三片词义场里的词。

normalIntro.en: Two Latin sources feed one spelling, and the senses sort themselves by which source they come from.
normalIntro.cn: 两条拉丁来源喂给同一个拼写，各个义项按来源自然分成两堆。

normal.en: The mail sense grows from posta, a relay station; letters moved from station to station along the road.
normal.cn: 邮政义出自 posta（驿站）；信件沿着大路一站一站往前传。

normal.en: The pole sense grows from postis, a doorpost, and has nothing to do with mail.
normal.cn: 柱子义出自 postis（门柱），与邮件毫无关系。

normal.en: Postage and postal keep the mail line, both built on post with different suffixes.
normal.cn: postage 与 postal 都留在邮政这条线上，只是加了不同后缀。

normal.en: A poster was first something posted up for people to read, before it meant a printed picture.
normal.cn: poster 最初指「张贴出来供人阅读的东西」，后来才指印刷的海报。

normal.en: To post a comment online repeats the old act of fixing a notice where others can see it.
normal.cn: 在网上 post 一条评论，重复的正是把告示固定在人人都看得见的地方。

abstract.en: A job post is a station for a person, just as a post was a station for a horse.
abstract.cn: 职位是人驻守的站点，正如当年的驿站是马匹换乘的站点。

abstract.en: Posting online is the village notice board moved onto a screen.

definition_zh: 英里；很长的距离；很大的差距
definition_en: a unit of distance of about one and six tenths kilometres; a long distance in everyday speech; and a large amount or degree of difference, especially in the phrase by a mile
core_image: 公路旁的里程碑立在草丛里，石面被风雨磨得发白，远处还有下一块
scene: 公路沿着荒原一直伸到天边，草丛里立着一块被风雨磨白的路碑，司机盯着它数着还有多远。 The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
sceneCN: 这里是「英里」（第 1 个义项：距离单位）；句意为过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里的路。图中可辨识物件：草丛里的路碑、伸向天边的公路、远处的弯道。

senses.title: A unit of distance used in Britain and America
senses.definition: a unit of distance used mainly in the United States and Britain, equal to about one and six tenths kilometres
senses.definitionCN: 主要在美国和英国使用的距离单位，约合一点六公里
senses.example: The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.
senses.exampleCN: 过了最后一个弯，下一座镇子还有一英里。
senses.why: The Latin phrase behind the word meant a thousand paces, so the mile began as a counted walk rather than an abstract length.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「一千步」，所以英里最初是一段数出来的路，而不是一个抽象的长度。

senses.title: A long distance in everyday speech
senses.definition: a long way, used loosely in conversation rather than as an exact measurement
senses.definitionCN: 口语中泛指很远的距离，并不作为精确度量
senses.example: From the hill you can see the sea, though it looks miles away.
senses.exampleCN: 从山上能看见海，虽然它看上去远得很。
senses.why: Because a mile is a noticeable stretch of road, the plural easily becomes a loose word for any distance that feels long.
senses.whyCN: 因为一英里是一段能明显感觉到的路，复数形式便很容易变成泛指「任何觉得远」的距离。

senses.title: A large amount or degree of difference
senses.definition: a great amount or degree of difference, especially in the phrase by a mile
senses.definitionCN: 差距或程度很大，尤用于短语 by a mile
senses.example: Her second design was better by a mile.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第二个设计要好得多。
senses.why: A race decided by a mile is decided by a visible stretch of road, so the word turns physical distance into the size of any gap.
senses.whyCN: 以「一英里」之差决出的比赛，是靠一段看得见的路来分胜负；于是这个词把物理距离变成了任何差距的大小。

intro.en: Mile comes from a Latin phrase for a thousand paces, shortened in English to a single word for a measured stretch of road.
intro.cn: mile 来自拉丁语中表示「一千步」的短语，在英语里缩略成一个词，指一段被丈量过的路。

items.en: Mille was the Latin word for a thousand, and it stood at the head of the phrase that named the Roman mile.
items.cn: mille 是拉丁语中表示「一千」的词，也是罗马「里」这一说法开头的词。

items.en: The full phrase milia passuum meant a thousand double paces, the Roman unit for a long march.
items.cn: 完整的短语 milia passuum 意为「一千个双步」，是罗马人计量长途行军的单位。

items.en: Old English borrowed the shortened form as mil, a unit of distance used in land measurement and travel.
items.cn: 古英语借入缩短后的形式 mil，用作丈量土地与旅行中的距离单位。

items.en: Middle English mile kept the unit, but its exact length still varied from place to place.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mile 保留了这一单位，但它确切的长度在各地方仍有差异。

items.en: Modern English fixed the mile at a standard length and added loose uses such as 「miles away」 and 「by a mile」.
items.cn: 现代英语把英里的长度固定下来，并发展出「miles away」「by a mile」这类宽泛用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the mile family and one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects other units of distance and the general idea of distance.
note.cn: 形近组收 mile 的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收其他距离单位以及「距离」这一总称。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin phrase for a thousand paces; its family keeps returning to measured road, marked stones and the loose feeling of somewhere far.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「一千步」的短语上；同族词反复回到被丈量的路、立在路边的石标，以及「很远」这种宽泛的感觉。

normal.en: Mille in Latin means a thousand, and milia passuum was a thousand paces.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mille 意为一千，milia passuum 就是一千个步子。

normal.en: The Roman mile was a counted march, which is why the word feels like a stretch of road rather than a number.
normal.cn: 罗马的「里」是一段数出来的行军路程，所以这个词感觉像一段路，而不是一个数字。

normal.en: Old English shortened the phrase to mil, and English kept only the unit, not the thousand.
normal.cn: 古英语把短语缩短成 mil，英语只留下单位，丢掉了「一千」这层意思。

normal.en: Milestone joins mile to stone, a real stone set beside the road to mark each mile.
normal.cn: milestone 把 mile 与 stone 组合，指路边为标记每英里而立的真石头。

normal.en: 「Miles away」 and 「by a mile」 loosen the unit into a picture of any long distance or wide gap.
normal.cn: 「miles away」与「by a mile」把这个单位放宽成任何长距离或大差距的画面。

abstract.en: A unit built from a thousand steps suggests that early measurement was simply walking, counted and named.
abstract.cn: 一个由「一千步」构成的单位说明：早期的度量不过是走路，数出来，再给它一个名字。

abstract.en: When a fixed mile becomes miles away, a precise unit turns into a human feeling of distance.
abstract.cn: 当固定的 mile 变成 miles away，精确的单位就变成了人对距离的感受。

abstract.en: By a mile measures a gap in road lengths, a reminder that we often describe victory as travelling further.
abstract.cn: by a mile 用路的长度衡量差距，这提醒人：我们常把胜利说成「走得更远」。

examples.en: The next town is still a mile beyond the last bend.

examples.en: From the hill you can see the sea, though it looks miles away.

examples.en: Her second design was better by a mile.
examples.cn: 她的第二个设计要好得多。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a counted march of a thousand paces; the senses divide into the fixed unit, the loose sense of a long way, and the size of a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一段数以千步计的行军路程；义项分为固定的距离单位、泛指「很远」，以及差距的大小。

definition_zh: 在国外；到国外；广泛地；流传开
definition_en: in or to a foreign country, or spread over a wide area
core_image: 机场里拖着行李准备出国的人
scene: 机场里，一个学生拖着行李准备出国读书。 She will study abroad next year.
sceneCN: 这里 abroad 是「到国外」（第 1 个义项：去外国）；句意为她明年将出国留学。

pos.zh: 副词：在国外；到国外；广泛地

derivatives.zh: 出国的说法

senses.title: In another country
senses.definition: in a country that is not one's own
senses.definitionCN: 在不是自己国家的国度里
senses.example: She has lived abroad for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她已在国外生活了两年。
senses.why: A- plus broad first meant out in the wide world, and it settled on being outside one's own country.
senses.whyCN: a- 加 broad 原指「在广阔的外面」，后来固定在「本国之外」。

senses.title: To another country
senses.definition: toward a country that is not one's own
senses.definitionCN: 朝着不是自己国家的方向
senses.example: They went abroad last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年夏天出国了。
senses.why: The same picture outside the country takes a direction of movement and becomes going abroad.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「在国外」的画面加上移动方向，就变成到国外去。

intro.en: The recorded history of abroad is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 abroad 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old phrase meant on broad or in a wide way.
items.cn: 古短语意为在宽广的范围上。

items.en: Broad supplied the sense of wide space, not of a country.
items.cn: broad 提供的是宽广空间的意思，而不是国家的意思。

items.en: The word shifted to mean outside one's own land.
items.cn: 这个词转而表示在自己国土之外。

items.en: Travel and trade made the foreign sense the main one.
items.cn: 旅行与贸易使「国外」成为主要义项。

items.en: Today it still keeps a second sense of widely spread.
items.cn: 今天它仍保留「广泛传开」这一次要义项。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The common verb phrase for leaving for another country.
entries.definitionCN: 表示出国常用的动词短语。

entries.definition: A set phrase for going to a foreign school.
entries.definitionCN: 表示到外国学校读书的固定说法。

entries.definition: A phrase for inside and outside the country.
entries.definitionCN: 表示国内与国外的短语。

entries.definition: It means across the sea, in a foreign land.
entries.definitionCN: 指跨过海洋，在外国。

entries.definition: It describes something of another country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容属于另一个国家的事物。

entries.definition: It means over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 指在大范围内或许多人中间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The old form meant wide, so abroad first meant widely, then outside the country.
normal.cn: 古词形意为宽广，所以 abroad 先表示广泛地，再表示在国外。

normal.en: The same family also gives go abroad and study abroad.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 go abroad 与 study abroad。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase study abroad.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「出国留学」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of abroad in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 abroad 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: in or to a foreign country, or spread over a wide area.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「在国外」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller at an airport with a suitcase, going abroad.
abstract.cn: 想象机场里拖着行李准备出国的人。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She has lived abroad for two years.
examples.cn: 她已在国外生活了两年。

examples.en: They went abroad last summer.
examples.cn: 他们去年夏天出国了。

examples.en: He hopes to study abroad after school.
examples.cn: 他希望毕业后到国外学习。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of abroad grows from one core image: a traveller at an airport with a suitcase, going abroad.
sensesIntro.cn: abroad 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：机场里拖着行李准备出国的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller at an airport with a suitcase, going abroad
core.cn: 核心意象：机场里拖着行李准备出国的人

branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：在国外。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: To another country.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：到国外。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: In another country / To another country.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：在国外、到国外。

branches.en: Sense 01 covers a later use: In another country.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖再往后的一种用法：在国外。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers the outer edge of the meaning: To another country.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖意义的边缘：到国外。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.

definition_zh: 性格；品质；人物；角色；汉字；符号
definition_en: the qualities that make a person special; a person in a story; a letter or symbol used in writing
core_image: 故事里那个一眼就能记住的人物，或方方正正的一个汉字
scene: 语文课上，老师让我们分析课文里小男孩的性格特点。 The main character in the story is a brave boy.
sceneCN: 这里 character 是「人物；角色」（第 2 个义项：故事中的人）；句意为故事的主人公是个勇敢的男孩。

pos.zh: 性格；品质；人物；角色；文字符号

derivatives.zh: 由 character 加 -ize 构成，义为「描绘……的特征」
由 character 加后缀构成，义为「典型的；特征」

senses.title: The qualities that make a person special
senses.definition: the mix of qualities that makes one person different from others
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人区别于他人的特质组合
senses.example: Hard work and honesty are part of her character.
senses.exampleCN: 勤奋与诚实是她品格的一部分。
senses.why: A tool's engraved mark fixed its identity; a person's qualities are the marks that fix theirs.
senses.whyCN: 刻印是器物的身份标记；人的特质正是标记其身份的「刻痕」。

senses.title: A person in a story or play
senses.definition: a person, animal or figure in a book, film or play
senses.definitionCN: 书、电影或戏剧中出现的人、动物或形象
senses.example: The main character in the story is a brave boy.
senses.exampleCN: 故事的主人公是个勇敢的男孩。
senses.why: The mark that fixes identity was given to the figures whose traits the writer engraves.
senses.whyCN: 用以标记身份的印记，被赋予了作家笔下刻画的形象。

senses.title: A letter, number or symbol used in writing
senses.definition: a letter, number or sign used in writing and printing
senses.definitionCN: 书写与印刷中使用的字母、数字或符号
senses.example: Chinese characters are written in square shapes.
senses.exampleCN: 汉字写成方块形状。
senses.why: Each written sign is a mark carved to fix a sound or meaning, the oldest sense at its most literal.
senses.whyCN: 每个文字符号都是刻下以固定音义的印记，是最古老义项最直接的呈现。

senses.title: A person with an unusual, striking nature
senses.definition: a person whose behaviour is amusing or unusual
senses.definitionCN: 举止有趣或与众不同的人
senses.example: Grandpa is quite a character at family dinners.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷在家庭聚餐上是个妙趣横生的人物。
senses.why: A person whose qualities are strongly marked stands out like a deep engraving.
senses.whyCN: 特质鲜明之人如深刻的刻痕般引人注目。

intro.en: Character comes from a Greek word for an engraving tool, growing into identity, story figures and written signs.
intro.cn: character 源自希腊语中指刻印工具的词，逐步生长为身份、故事人物与文字符号之义。

items.en: Greek kharakter meant an engraving tool, and the mark it makes.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 指刻印工具及其刻下的印记。

items.en: Late Latin character meant an engraved mark or a written sign.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 character 指刻印的标记或书写的符号。

items.en: Old French caractère carried the mark sense into Europe's languages.
items.cn: 古法语 caractère 把标记之义带入欧洲诸语言。

items.en: Middle English character meant a written sign, then a person's qualities.
items.cn: 中古英语 character 先指文字符号，后指人的品质。

items.en: Modern English uses character for personality, story figures and letters.
items.cn: 现代英语的 character 兼指性格、故事人物与文字。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects people and signs.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收人物与符号类词。

entries.definition: Typical of a person or thing.

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宪章」，拼写与 character 词首相近。

entries.definition: The whole nature of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「个性」，与 character 的性格义相近。

entries.definition: A part played in a film or play.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「角色」，与 character 的角色义相近。

entries.definition: A sign that stands for something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「符号」，与 character 的符号义相近。
