definition_zh: 年少的；初级的；资历较浅的；下级的；职位低的；较年轻者
definition_en: younger in age, or lower in rank or experience than someone else
core_image: 队列里排在后面、个子还矮一头的那个新人
scene: 办公室里最新的那个人坐在靠门的位置，桌上只摆着一台旧电脑。 As a junior clerk, he handled the files nobody else wanted.
sceneCN: 这里 junior 是「初级的、资历浅的」（第 1 个义项：在职位或经验上低于他人），句意为作为初级职员，他处理没人愿意管的档案。画面里的物件：办公室、靠门的桌子、旧电脑。

pos.zh: 形容词：年少的；初级的；资历浅的；下级的
名词：较年轻者；下级；初级职员

derivatives.zh: 由 junior 加 -ity 构成，义为「资历较浅的状态」
由 junior 加 -ate 构成，指修会培养期或初级阶段

senses.title: Lower in rank or experience
senses.definition: having a lower position or less experience than others in the same organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一机构中职位较低或经验较少
senses.example: She started as a junior designer in the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工作室从初级设计师做起。
senses.why: Rank is the comparison that matters most in offices, staff against staff.
senses.whyCN: 在办公室里最重要的比较是职位，是员工与员工之间的比较。

senses.title: Younger in age
senses.definition: younger than another person, often used of a son named after his father
senses.definitionCN: 年龄小于他人，常用于父子同名的场合
senses.example: He is three years junior to his brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他比哥哥小三岁。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply younger, and it still keeps the Latin comparison.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层意思就是「更年轻」，它仍保留着拉丁语比较级的底子。

senses.title: Of the lower school level
senses.definition: relating to the earlier part of a school or a college year
senses.definitionCN: 指学校的低年级阶段或大学三年级
senses.example: She teaches at a junior school near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 她在公园附近的一所小学教书。
senses.why: Schools borrow the age comparison and turn it into a stage of study.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了年龄比较，把它变成一个学段。

senses.title: A person of lower rank
senses.definition: a person who holds a lower position than someone else
senses.definitionCN: 职位低于他人的人
senses.example: The partners rarely listen to the juniors.
senses.exampleCN: 合伙人很少听下属的意见。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a person: the lower-ranked member of the team.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成一个人：团队中位次较低的那个成员。

senses.title: Smaller in a competition class
senses.definition: belonging to a younger age group in sport or contests
senses.definitionCN: 指体育或竞赛中属于较年轻年龄组
senses.example: He won the junior title at fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十五岁就拿下了少年组冠军。
senses.why: Sport turns age into a class, with its own titles and records.
senses.whyCN: 体育把年龄变成一个组别，有自己的冠军和纪录。

senses.title: The third college year
senses.definition: in American usage, the third year of a four-year course
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指四年制课程的第三年
senses.example: She spent her junior year abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她大三那年去了国外。
senses.why: In a four-year course the third year is junior to the last one.
senses.whyCN: 在四年制课程里，第三年比上年一级「低」，于是叫 junior year。

intro.en: Junior was borrowed from Latin junior, the comparative of juvenis, young; English uses it unchanged.
intro.cn: junior 直接借自拉丁语 junior，是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级；英语原样沿用。

items.en: juvenis meant young, and junior was its comparative form.
items.cn: juvenis 意为年轻的，junior 是它的比较级。

items.en: The -or ending marks the comparative, as in senior.
items.cn: -or 词尾标记比较级，senior 也是如此。

items.en: English borrowed junior in the sixteenth century as an adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 junior，兼作形容词和名词。

items.en: The rank sense spread through offices and armed forces.
items.cn: 「职位较低」这一义在机关和军队中扩散。

items.en: The school senses, junior school and junior year, settled in the modern period.
items.cn: 初级学校与大学三年级等教育义在近现代固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin comparatives that end in -or; the near-meaning group holds words for younger and lower rank.
note.cn: 形近组收以 -or 结尾的拉丁比较级；近义组收表示年幼与低级的词。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank.
entries.definitionCN: junior 的反义对应词，义为「年长的；高级的」。

entries.definition: Young, or a young person.
entries.definitionCN: 同源于 juvenis，义为「少年的」。

entries.definition: The state of being junior.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，指资历较浅的状态。

entries.definition: Less old than another person.
entries.definitionCN: 最简单直白的「更年轻的」。

entries.definition: Lower in rank within a system.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指体制中下级。

entries.definition: Someone being trained for a job.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在受训的岗位新人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin comparative ending to the desk by the door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语比较级词尾走到靠门的那张桌子。

normal.en: Junior is the comparative of juvenis, young.
normal.cn: junior 是 juvenis「年轻」的比较级。

normal.en: The pair junior and senior is fixed in offices and schools.
normal.cn: junior 与 senior 这一对在机关和学校都固定。

normal.en: Junior to someone uses to, not than.
normal.cn: junior to someone 用 to，不用 than。

normal.en: Junior high school covers the early teenage years.
normal.cn: junior high school 指初中阶段。

normal.en: In American colleges junior year is the third year.
normal.cn: 美国大学的 junior year 是第三年。

abstract.en: A junior is one row back in the same line.
abstract.cn: 初级者是在同一条队伍里后退一排的人。

abstract.en: The word is a comparison, so it always needs another person.
abstract.cn: 这个词是比较，因此总需要另一个人才成立。

abstract.en: Everyone is junior to someone, and senior to someone else.
abstract.cn: 每个人对某些人初级，对另一些人高级。

examples.en: Two junior staff members handled the whole report.
examples.cn: 两名初级员工完成了整份报告。

examples.en: My sister is junior to me by two years.
examples.cn: 我妹妹比我小两岁。

examples.en: He is looking for a junior position in design.
examples.cn: 他在找一个设计方面的初级职位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「就是你儿」—— 家里年纪最小的那个，就是初级选手

root: 拉丁语 juvenis「年轻的」→ 比较级 junior → 英语 junior，原样借用；同族的反义比较级是 senior。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: lower rank, younger age, lower school level, a lower-ranked person, a younger contest class, and the third college year.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：职位较低、年纪较小、学校初段、下级人员、少年组，以及大学三年级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person standing a row behind and half a head lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在后退一排、矮半头的位置。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a new desk and the files nobody wants.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：新桌子与没人要的档案。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the son who shares the father's name.
branches.cn: 家庭这条线：与父亲同名的儿子。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: early years and the third college year.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：低年级与大学三年级。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the younger age bracket of a contest.
branches.cn: 赛场这条线：比赛的较年轻年龄组。

branches.en: THE LADDER: every rung is junior to the one above.
branches.cn: 梯子这条线：每一级都低于它上面那一级。

intro.en: Junior is a Latin comparative borrowed whole; English adds only a few endings.
intro.cn: junior 是整体借来的拉丁比较级，英语只添了少数词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all grow from juvenis, young.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都从 juvenis「年轻」长出来。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 junior 与 senior。

items.example: More junior is the periphrastic form.
items.exampleCN: more junior 是分析式比较级。

definition_zh: 海报；招贴画；张贴者
definition_en: a large printed notice or picture put up in a public place; a person who posts letters or messages
core_image: 车站墙上贴着一张大海报，颜色鲜艳，路过的人都忍不住多看一眼
scene: 车站大厅的墙上新贴了一张电影宣传画。 A colorful poster by the ticket office promised that the film would open next week.
sceneCN: 这里 poster 是「海报、招贴画」（第 1 个义项：贴在公共场所的大幅印刷品）；句意为售票处旁一张色彩鲜艳的海报预告电影下周上映。

pos.zh: 海报；招贴画；贴在墙上的大幅印刷品

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「邮政；柱子；（网络）帖子」，也是动词「张贴；邮寄」
由 post 加 -age 构成，义为「邮资」
由 poster 与 board 复合而成，义为「海报纸板」

senses.title: A large printed notice for public display
senses.definition: a large printed sheet of paper with a picture or announcement, put up where many people will see it
senses.definitionCN: 印着图画或告示的大幅印刷品，贴在很多人能看到的地方
senses.example: They put up posters to advertise the school concert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们贴出海报为学校音乐会做宣传。
senses.why: To post is to fix something where the public passes; a poster is simply the large sheet that gets posted.
senses.whyCN: post 作动词是把东西固定在公众来往之处，poster 就是那张被贴上去的大纸。

senses.title: A person who posts
senses.definition: a person who posts letters, notices or messages, now often someone who publishes content online
senses.definitionCN: 张贴信件、告示或发送消息的人，现在常指在网上发布内容的人
senses.example: The forum ranks its most active posters every month.
senses.exampleCN: 论坛每月给最活跃的发帖人排名。
senses.why: Adding -er to post names the doer of the action, so the word follows the person wherever posting happens, from a notice board to a forum.
senses.whyCN: post 加 -er 构成动作执行者，于是这个词跟着「张贴」这个动作走，从布告栏一直走到论坛。

intro.en: Poster is built on post, an English word with two Latin sources: the postal sense runs from ponere, the upright-stake sense from popularis, and the poster we hang came through the mailing sense.
intro.cn: poster 建立在 post 之上；post 有两个拉丁来源：邮政义来自 ponere（放置），立柱义来自 popularis，而海报义走的是邮寄这一路。

items.en: Latin ponere meant to place, to put; from it came pausare, to halt, and the idea of setting something down.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置、安放，由此派生出 pausare（停驻），以及「把某物安放下来」的观念。

items.en: Medieval Latin postare gave post, first the fixed stations where mail was set down and changed horses, then the mail itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 postare 给出 post，先指放置邮件、换马的固定驿站，后指邮件本身。

items.en: Old French poste carried both the fixed station and the mail that moved between stations; it also named an upright stake, a separate Latin line from popularis.
items.cn: 古法语 poste 兼指固定驿站和往来其间的邮件；它还指立柱，那来自另一条拉丁语线索 popularis。

items.en: English post covered the mail, an upright stake, and the act of fixing a notice where the public passes.
items.cn: 英语的 post 兼指邮件、立柱，以及把告示固定在公众经过之处的动作。

items.en: From post came poster, first the person who posts, then the large printed sheet meant to be posted on walls; today it also names online content images.
items.cn: 由 post 派生出 poster，先指张贴者，后指专供张贴的大幅印刷品；如今也指网上的图片内容。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the post family and one word that only echoes the ending; the near-meaning group gathers printed things meant for the public eye.
note.cn: 形近组收 post 词族的词，另收一个只是词尾相像的词；近义组收面向公众的各类印刷品。

entries.definition: The mail, an upright stake, or the act of fixing a notice; the first element of poster.
entries.definitionCN: 邮件、立柱，或张贴告示的动作；poster 的基础词。

entries.definition: The charge for sending mail, built on post with the suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 邮寄费用；由 post 加后缀 -age 构成。

entries.definition: The act of posting a letter or publishing an online message.
entries.definitionCN: 投寄信件或发布网络消息的行为。

entries.definition: A list of names and duties; it echoes the -ster ending but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 值班名单；词尾与 poster 相像，来源不同。

entries.definition: A written or printed announcement put up for people to read.
entries.definitionCN: 张贴出来供人阅读的书面告示。

entries.definition: A printed notice or advertisement, especially one posted in public.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷的告示或广告，尤指贴在公共场所的。

entries.definition: A displayed board or notice giving information or directions.
entries.definitionCN: 提供信息或指引的展示牌、标牌。

normalIntro.en: Everything in the word points back to post: the sheet is made to be posted, and the person is the one who posts it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的一切都回指 post：那张纸是为张贴而做的，那个人是执行张贴的人。

normal.en: Poster = post + er: first the doer, then the thing that gets done to, a sheet for posting.
normal.cn: poster = post + er：先指做动作的人，后指承受动作的东西，即供张贴的大纸。

normal.en: Post ultimately traces to Latin ponere, to place: a poster is simply a picture placed on public view.
normal.cn: post 最终可溯至拉丁语 ponere（放置）：海报就是被放到公众视野里的一幅画。

normal.en: To post a letter and to post a notice use the same word; a poster is the notice enlarged.
normal.cn: 寄信和张贴告示用的是同一个动词；海报就是放大了的告示。

normal.en: The plural is regular: poster becomes posters.
normal.cn: 复数规则变化：poster 变 posters。

normal.en: Online posters are the modern heirs: same word, new wall, the screen.
normal.cn: 网络发帖人是它的现代后裔：同一个词，换了一堵新墙——屏幕。

abstract.en: A poster is a wall speaking: it shouts one picture and five words to everyone passing.
abstract.cn: 海报是一面会说话的墙：向每个路过的人喊出一幅图和五个词。

abstract.en: Posters sell dreams at the height of the eye, exactly where you look while waiting.
abstract.cn: 海报在视线的高度出售梦想，恰好是你等候时会看的地方。

abstract.en: A city without posters is a room with nothing on its walls.
abstract.cn: 没有海报的城市，像一堵什么都不挂的墙围成的房间。

examples.en: They put up posters to advertise the school concert.
examples.cn: 他们贴出海报为学校音乐会做宣传。

examples.en: A colorful poster by the ticket office promised that the film would open next week.
examples.cn: 售票处旁一张色彩鲜艳的海报预告电影下周上映。

examples.en: He designed a poster for the sports meet and posted it near the gate.
examples.cn: 他为运动会设计了一张海报，贴在大门附近。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖斯特」——把海报「剖」开来「贴」上墙，路人都「特」别爱看，这就是 poster。

root: poster 由 post 加执行者后缀 -er 构成；post 经中世纪拉丁语 postare 与古法语 poste 进入英语，邮政义可溯至拉丁语 ponere（放置），立柱义另有来源 popularis，两条线索在古法语交汇。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sheet fixed where the public passes; the senses run from the printed notice itself to the person who posts letters or messages.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是固定在公众必经之处的一张大纸；义项从印好的招贴本身，走到投寄信件、发布消息的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright sheet pasted on a station wall, read by everyone who waits.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站墙上一张鲜亮的纸，等车的人都看它。

branches.en: a film poster by the ticket office
branches.cn: 售票处的电影海报

branches.en: concert posters pasted across campus
branches.cn: 贴满校园的音乐会海报

branches.en: the worker posting bills on the hoarding
branches.cn: 往围板上贴告示的工人

branches.en: an active poster in an online forum
branches.cn: 论坛里活跃的发帖人

branches.en: posters calling for volunteers, posted and reposted
branches.cn: 招募志愿者的海报，贴了又贴

intro.en: The word is a plain English derivation, but its base post carries two Latin lines that met in Old French.
intro.cn: 这个词是简单的英语派生词，但它的基础词 post 带着两条在古法语交汇的拉丁线索。

latinIntro.en: The postal line runs through Medieval Latin postare from ponere; that chain is recorded and listed as the Latin entries.
latinIntro.cn: 邮政一条线经中世纪拉丁语 postare 上溯 ponere；这条链条有据可查，列为拉丁条目。

items.meaning: mail, stake, to fix a notice
a person who does the action
a large printed notice to be posted

latinEntries.meaning: to place at stations, to halt

definition_zh: 例子；实例；榜样；范例；样板
definition_en: a thing or person that is typical of a group, or a model that shows how something should be done
core_image: 货架上的样品：拿一个具体的东西放在你眼前，让你看清整类东西的样子
scene: 老师讲到几何题，班上没人听懂，她只好在黑板上画了一个三角形，边写边说： Let me give you an example so you can see how the rule works.
sceneCN: 这里 example 指「用来演示规则的例子」（第 1 个义项：说明某类事物的具体实例）；句意为老师举一个三角形的例子帮学生看懂规则。

derivatives.zh: 举例说明；是…的典型（example 加动词后缀 -ify，义为「拿例子来证明」）
可作楷模的；典范的（example 加形容词后缀 -ary，义为「堪称榜样的」）
模范；典型样本（拉丁词形直入英语，义为「被拿出来当样本的东西」）

senses.title: A concrete instance of a group or rule
senses.titleCN: 说明某类事物的具体实例
senses.definition: one particular thing that is taken from a group to show what the whole group is like
senses.definitionCN: 从一群同类事物中拿出一个具体的东西，用来展示这一整类的样子
senses.example: Let me give you an example so you can see how the rule works.
senses.exampleCN: 我举一个例子，好让你看懂这条规则怎么用。
senses.why: The core image is a sample on display: you cannot see an abstract rule directly, so you hold up one concrete case and let it stand for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是货架上的样品：抽象规则看不见，只能拿出一个具体案例，让它替整类东西说话。

senses.title: A person worthy of imitation
senses.definition: a person or behaviour that other people should try to copy because it is good
senses.definitionCN: 因为做得好而值得别人学着做的人或行为
senses.example: A good captain sets an example for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好队长会给全队树立榜样。
senses.why: When the sample is a person, the case on display is not just descriptive but prescriptive: others are expected to copy it.
senses.whyCN: 当「样品」换成人，摆出来的案例就不只是描述，还带上了要求：别人应该照着做。

senses.title: A warning instance
senses.definition: an instance of bad behaviour or failure that shows others what to avoid
senses.definitionCN: 用一件坏事或一次失败给旁人看，提醒他们别重蹈覆辙
senses.example: The judge made the punishment an example to future offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 法官重罚这名犯人，让后来的人引以为戒。
senses.why: A displayed case can point two ways: it can show what to copy, or what to avoid; the direction comes from context.
senses.whyCN: 摆出来的案例有两个指向：既可以是让人学的好样子，也可以是让人躲的坏下场；方向由语境决定。

senses.title: A problem to be solved as practice
senses.definition: a question or problem worked out as a model for learners to follow
senses.definitionCN: 把一道题完整解出来，给学习者照着做的一道示范题
senses.example: The textbook shows a worked example before each exercise set.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书在每组练习前都给出例题的完整解法。
senses.why: In teaching, the sample case is a solved problem: the learner first watches the rule in action, then repeats it alone.
senses.whyCN: 在教学里，样品就是解好的一道题：学习者先看规则运行一遍，再自己重复一遍。

senses.title: A typical representative of a kind
senses.definition: a thing that fairly represents the typical qualities of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 能公平代表某一类东西典型特征的物件
senses.example: This old machine is a fine example of early engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧机器是早期工程技术的优秀代表。
senses.why: The sample stands for the whole group only if it is typical; so an example also carries the meaning of a fair representative.
senses.whyCN: 样品要能代表全体，前提是它够典型；所以 example 也带上「典型代表」的意思。

intro.en: Example runs straight back to Latin, through French, and its root image is "taking something out" to be seen.
intro.cn: example 一路源自拉丁语、经古法语进入英语，词根画面是「把某样东西拿出来」给人看。

items.en: Latin exemplum meant "a sample, a pattern, a warning case", from eximere "to take out", built on ex- (out) + emere (to take).
items.cn: 拉丁语 exemplum 意为「样品、范例、警示案例」，来自 eximere「取出」，由 ex-（向外）+ emere（拿）构成。

items.en: The underlying image is literally taking one item out of a pile so that it can be examined as a stand-in for the rest.
items.cn: 底层画面就是从一堆东西里拿出一件，让它充当其余物品的代表接受检视。

items.en: Old French carried the word as essample / example, keeping the sense of model and warning.
items.cn: 古法语以 essample / example 的形式继承了这个词，保留了「模范」「警示」的意思。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it from French as example by the thirteenth century, covering both instance and model.
items.cn: 十三世纪中古英语从法语借入 example，同时覆盖「实例」与「典范」两义。

items.en: Modern English kept both lines: a neutral instance to clarify, and a model to imitate or a warning to avoid.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两条线：用来讲清楚的中性实例，以及供效仿的模范或供引以为戒的警示。

note.en: The words below are close to example in spelling or in the idea of a displayed case.
note.cn: 下面的词在拼写上或「摆出案例给人看」这层意思上与 example 相近。

entries.definition: a model or ideal pattern worth copying
entries.definitionCN: 模范；理想范式（与 example 同根，拉丁词形直接入英语）

entries.definition: serving as a desirable model; very good
entries.definitionCN: 堪称典范的（同根形容词）

entries.definition: free from an obligation or duty required of others
entries.definitionCN: 被免除的（拼写相近但词根不同，来自 exonera 一族，义为「免除」）

entries.definition: a small part taken to show what the whole is like
entries.definitionCN: 样品；样本（与 example 同源于拉丁 eximere）

entries.definition: a single case of something happening
entries.definitionCN: 一个具体事例（强调事件性的一次）

entries.definition: a standard thing to copy
entries.definitionCN: 典范；模型（强调「值得照着做」）

entries.definition: an example that makes a point clearer
entries.definitionCN: 说明性实例（为讲清观点而举）

normalIntro.en: Five steady associations built from the real word family and collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词族与搭配的稳当联想。

normal.en: ex- means out, so an example is a case taken out of the group for display.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 表示「向外」，example 就是「从一堆里拿出来展示」的那一件。

normal.en: Give an example: teachers hold up one triangle to stand for all triangles.
normal.cn: 举例子：老师举一个三角形，让它代表所有三角形。

normal.en: Set an example: a good captain is also a displayed sample of behaviour.
normal.cn: 树立榜样：好队长本身就是被摆出来的「行为样品」。

normal.en: Exemplify is the verb twin: one clear case exemplifies the rule.
normal.cn: exemplify 是动词孪生词：一个清楚的案例就能证明规则。

normal.en: For example is the everyday hinge that opens any clarification.
normal.cn: for example 是日常口头禅，一说出口就开始举例讲清楚。

abstract.en: Picture a shop shelf: one item is pulled forward under a spotlight as the sample.
abstract.cn: 想象一个货架：一件商品被拉到聚光灯下当样品。

abstract.en: The spotlight case can shine as a hero to copy or as a warning to avoid.
abstract.cn: 聚光灯下的案例可以是供效仿的英雄，也可以是供引以为戒的反面教材。

abstract.en: An abstract rule has no face until one example gives it a body.
abstract.cn: 抽象规则原本没有面孔，直到一个例子给它安上血肉。

examples.en: Let me give you an example so you can see how the rule works.
examples.cn: 我举一个例子，好让你看懂这条规则怎么用。

examples.en: A good captain sets an example for the whole team.
examples.cn: 一个好队长会给全队树立榜样。

examples.en: This old machine is a fine example of early engineering.
examples.cn: 这台旧机器是早期工程技术的优秀代表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个赞助普」——有人赞助了一件普通样品，把它摆在最显眼的位置当例子。

root: 源自拉丁语 exemplum「样品、范例」，来自动词 eximere「取出」，由 ex-（向外）+ emere（拿、取）构成；一般认为 emere 在此取「拿到手」义。经古法语 essample 进入中古英语后拼成 example。

sensesIntro.en: From a concrete case held up for inspection, the word widens into models to copy and warning cases to avoid.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个被拿出来检视的具体案例，扩展到供效仿的典范与供引以为戒的警示案例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one case pulled out of the group and put on display
core.cn: 核心意象：从一堆同类中拉出一件，摆出来给人看

branches.en: the displayed case clarifies a rule
branches.cn: 摆出来的案例把规则讲清楚

branches.en: the case becomes a model to imitate
branches.cn: 案例变成供效仿的典范

branches.en: the case becomes a warning to avoid
branches.cn: 案例变成供引以为戒的警示

branches.en: the case fairly stands for its kind
branches.cn: 案例公平地代表它的类别

branches.en: sampling logic: one part speaks for the whole
branches.cn: 取样逻辑：以部分代言整体

intro.en: The example family is small but regular, all built on the Latin root em- (take) with ex- (out).
intro.cn: example 词族不大但规律清晰，全部建立在拉丁词根 em-（拿取）加 ex-（向外）之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins that keep the "take out" root.

definition_zh: 混合物；混合；混合料；交织的情感
definition_en: a combination of different things; also the act of combining them, a prepared blend, and a mingling of feelings
core_image: 一只碗里倒进面粉、水与糖，几样东西被搅成一体，分不清彼此
scene: 厨房的台面上摊着面粉、鸡蛋和牛奶，一只手把碗里的东西搅得越来越匀。 With a few quick strokes, the mixture in the bowl became smooth and pale.
sceneCN: 这里是「混合物、搅好的东西」（第 1 个义项：由不同成分合在一起的整体）；句意为搅了几下，碗里的混合物就变得细腻发白。图中可辨识物件：面碗、木勺、散落的面粉。

pos.zh: 混合物；混合；混合料；交织的情感

derivatives.zh: 与 mixture 同出拉丁语 miscere（混合），经中古英语 mixen 简化为动词，义为「混合」
由 mix 加表示「做某事的工具或人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「搅拌器；调音台」
由 mix 加 -ing 构成，义为「混合；混音」
由 ad-（附加）加拉丁语 mixtura 构成，义为「掺入物；附加成分」

senses.title: A combination of different substances
senses.definition: something made by putting two or more different substances or things together
senses.definitionCN: 两种或更多不同物质合在一起形成的东西
senses.example: Stir the mixture until the sugar dissolves.
senses.exampleCN: 把混合物搅拌到糖完全溶解。
senses.why: Latin mixtura named the result of miscere, the act of stirring things together, so the noun was born pointing at the finished blend rather than at the stirring.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mixtura 指 miscere（把东西搅到一起）的结果，所以这个名词从一开始就指搅好的成品，而不是指搅这个动作。

senses.title: The act of bringing things together
senses.definition: the process of putting different things together so that they combine
senses.definitionCN: 把不同东西放到一起使它们合成一体的过程
senses.example: The recipe calls for a slow mixture of butter and flour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个配方要求把黄油与面粉慢慢地混合。
senses.why: The same Latin stem could name the deed as well as its result, and English kept both, so one word covers the stirring and the thing stirred.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词干既能指动作，也能指动作的结果，英语把两者都留了下来，于是一个词既管搅拌这个动作，也管搅出来的东西。

senses.title: A blend prepared for cooking or medicine
senses.definition: a combination of ingredients prepared for a particular purpose, especially in baking or as a medicine
senses.definitionCN: 为某个具体用途按配方调好的多种成分，尤用于烘焙或作药
senses.example: The chemist measured a cough mixture into a small brown bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师把止咳药水量进一只棕色小瓶。
senses.why: From blends in general the word narrowed to blends made for a use: flour and eggs for a cake, drugs and syrup for a cough, each following its own recipe.
senses.whyCN: 从泛指的混合物，词义收窄到为某个用途调配的混合物：做蛋糕的面粉鸡蛋、治咳嗽的药与糖浆，各自按自己的配方来。

senses.title: A mingling of feelings
senses.definition: a combination of different feelings or qualities that appear together
senses.definitionCN: 不同情感或特质同时出现、彼此掺杂的状态
senses.example: She spoke with a mixture of relief and regret.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话时带着宽慰与懊悔交织的心情。
senses.why: A blend does not have to be physical: once the word meant any combined whole, it could hold invisible ingredients such as relief and regret in one sentence.
senses.whyCN: 混合物不必是实物：当这个词可以泛指任何合成的整体，它就能在同一句里装下宽慰与懊悔这些看不见的成分。

intro.en: Mixture comes from Latin mixtura, a noun of result built on the verb miscere, and it entered English through French with the sense of a blended whole.
intro.cn: mixture 来自拉丁语 mixtura，这个名词由动词 miscere 的「结果」义构成，经法语进入英语，意为混合成的整体。

items.en: Miscere meant to mix, stir or mingle, and it described liquids as well as, figuratively, people and affairs.
items.cn: miscere 意为混合、搅动、掺在一起，既用于液体，也比喻用于人和事务。

items.en: Its past participle mixtus meant having been mixed, and that form supplied the stem for the nouns built on the result.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 mixtus 意为「已被混合的」，为后来表示结果的各名词提供了词干。

items.en: Mixtura added the noun suffix -tura to the participle stem and named the thing produced by mixing.
items.cn: mixtura 在分词词干后加名词后缀 -tura，指混合之后产生的东西。

items.en: Old French took the noun as mixture and passed it into English in the fourteenth century alongside learned borrowings from Latin.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词作 mixture，在十四世纪随拉丁语借词一起传入英语。

items.en: English widened mixture from substances to recipes and medicines, then to feelings and qualities that appear together.
items.cn: 英语把 mixture 从物质扩展到配方与药水，再扩展到同时出现的情感与特质。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin verb of mixing; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for combined wholes in chemistry, cooking and everyday speech.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「混合」动词的同族词；近义组收化学、烹饪与日常说法里表示合成整体的名词。

entries.definition: To put different things together so that they form one mass.
entries.definitionCN: 把不同东西放在一起，使它们成为一体。

entries.definition: A machine or device that stirs ingredients together.
entries.definitionCN: 把原料搅在一起的机器或器具。

entries.definition: Something added to a main substance in a smaller amount.
entries.definitionCN: 以较少分量掺入主要物质的东西。

entries.definition: A mixture of two or more things that go well together.
entries.definitionCN: 两种或更多彼此协调的东西混合成的整体。

entries.definition: A substance formed from two or more elements or parts.
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或更多成分构成的物质。

entries.definition: A metal made by melting two or more metals together.
entries.definitionCN: 把两种或更多金属熔在一起制成的金属。

entries.definitionCN: 把分开的事物合成一种安排的结果。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of stirring, and its family keeps returning to the act of mixing and to the thing that mixing leaves behind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「搅拌」动词上，同族词反复回到搅拌这个动作，以及搅拌之后留下的东西。

normal.en: Miscere in Latin means to mix, so mixture rests on the act of stirring, not on any single ingredient.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 miscere 意为混合，所以 mixture 依托的是「搅」这个动作，而不是某一种原料。

normal.en: -tura is a Latin noun ending for the result of an action, so mixtura is literally the thing that mixing leaves behind.
normal.cn: -tura 是拉丁语里表示动作结果的名词词尾，所以 mixtura 字面就是「搅拌之后留下的东西」。

normal.en: Mix, mixer and admixture share the same stem, which is why one Latin verb yields a verb, a tool and an added element.
normal.cn: mix、mixer 与 admixture 共用同一个词干，所以一个拉丁动词能长出动词、工具和掺入物三种词。

normal.en: A cough mixture and a cake mixture follow one pattern: a list of ingredients turned into something usable.
normal.cn: 止咳药水和蛋糕面糊是同一个路子：一张配料清单变成一样可用的东西。

normal.en: A mixture of relief and regret shows that the word needs no physical ingredients, since feelings can be blended too.
normal.cn: 「宽慰与懊悔的混合」说明这个词不必有实物成分，情感也能被搅在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl where flour, water and sugar lose their outlines and become one pale mass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，面粉、水与糖各自失去轮廓，变成一整团浅色的东西。

abstract.en: Every mixture keeps traces of its parts: you can still taste each ingredient after they merge.
abstract.cn: 每个混合物都留着各成分的痕迹：合成一体之后，仍能尝出每一种原料。

abstract.en: A word born from stirring shows that English often names a whole by the action that produced it.
abstract.cn: 一个从「搅」里出生的词说明，英语常用产生整体的那个动作来给整体命名。

examples.en: Stir the mixture until the sugar dissolves.
examples.cn: 把混合物搅拌到糖完全溶解。

examples.en: She spoke with a mixture of relief and regret.
examples.cn: 她说话时带着宽慰与懊悔交织的心情。

examples.en: The pharmacist shook the bottle before pouring the mixture.
examples.cn: 药剂师倒药水之前先摇了摇瓶子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米克斯扯」——几样东西被米克在一起，扯也扯不开；记住 mixture 是混合物，也可指药水与心情的掺杂。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是混合成的整体；义项由此分出搅拌的动作、按配方调好的混合料，以及情感的交织。

definition_zh: 祝贺；恭喜；向……道贺
definition_en: to tell someone you are pleased about their success or good luck

scene: 小林在作文比赛中得了一等奖，全班都为他高兴。 We all congratulated him after the results were announced.

senses.title: To express joy at someone's success

senses.definition: to say you are pleased about someone's success or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的成功或成就表示高兴
senses.example: The teacher congratulated us on winning the basketball final.
senses.exampleCN: 老师祝贺我们赢得篮球决赛。
senses.why: The Latin root means to rejoice together, so congratulating is sharing another person's joy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义是一同高兴，所以祝贺就是分享他人的喜悦。

senses.title: To praise someone for good luck or an event
senses.definition: to offer good words about a happy event such as a birth or a promotion
senses.definitionCN: 对喜事如升学、升职等送上祝福
senses.example: Everyone congratulated her when she passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过考试时大家都向她道贺。
senses.why: Happy events invite shared joy, and the verb covers these everyday celebrations too.
senses.whyCN: 喜事让人想一同庆祝，这个词也覆盖这些日常的庆祝场合。

senses.title: To express sympathy about avoiding trouble
senses.titleCN: 庆幸；为躲过麻烦而道贺
senses.definition: to say someone was lucky to avoid something bad
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人幸运地躲过了坏事
senses.example: I congratulated myself on catching the early bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我庆幸自己赶上了早班车。

senses.whyCN: 分享喜悦是双向的：甚至可以为自己躲过一劫而暗自庆幸。

intro.en: Congratulate literally means to rejoice together with someone.

items.en: The Latin verb congratulari meant to rejoice with, from gratus (pleasing) + com- (with).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 congratulari 意为与人同乐，由 gratus（令人高兴）+ com-（共同）构成。

items.en: Medieval scholars used congratulatio for the act of expressing joy.
items.cn: 中世纪学者用 congratulatio 表示表达喜悦的行为。

items.en: French carried congratulacion into the language of scholars.
items.cn: 法语把 congratulacion 带进了学术语言。

items.en: English adopted congratulate in the sixteenth century as a learned word.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 congratulate，当时是书面用词。

items.en: Today it is a polite everyday verb, and congratulations is a common cheer.
items.cn: 如今它是礼貌的日常动词，congratulations 更成了常用的喝彩语。

note.en: These words share the grat root of joy, or mark similar celebrations.
note.cn: 这些词共享表示「高兴」的 grat 词根，或表示类似的祝贺。

examples.en: Let me congratulate you on your new school record.
examples.cn: 恭喜你刷新了校纪录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯捉了贴」——肯为获奖同学捉来彩带贴横幅，一起道贺。

root: 拉丁语 congratulari（与人同乐），由 com-（共同）+ gratus（令人高兴的）构成。grat 词根同族词有 grateful（感激的）、gratitude（感恩）、gratify（使满意）。

sensesIntro.en: From shared joy to celebrations and self-relief.
sensesIntro.cn: 从与人同乐延伸到庆祝喜事和自我庆幸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rejoicing together
core.cn: 核心意象：与人同乐

branches.en: Sharing joy at success.
branches.cn: 为成功分享喜悦。

branches.en: Congratulating on happy events.
branches.cn: 为喜事道贺。

branches.en: Feeling lucky to escape trouble.
branches.cn: 为躲过麻烦而庆幸。

branches.en: Good news calls for shared words.
branches.cn: 好消息需要彼此道贺。

branches.en: Joy can point inward too.
branches.cn: 喜悦也可以指向自己。

intro.en: The grat root of pleasing links a family of happy words.
intro.cn: grat（令人高兴）词根连接了一族表示喜悦的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratus means pleasing or thankful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gratus 意为令人高兴的、感激的。

items.exampleCN: 好消息让每个人都很高兴。

items.exampleCN: 他们整晚都在庆祝胜利。

She showed gratitude with a card.

definition_zh: 医疗的；医学的；内科的；身体状况的；（名词）体检
definition_en: relating to the practice, profession or study of medicine, to treatment that is not surgical, or to a person's health and health records
core_image: 白大褂口袋里露出一截听诊器，背后夹着一叠病历
scene: 她车里放着急救箱，包里带着医院的病历。 She kept a medical kit in the car and a copy of her hospital records in her bag.
sceneCN: 这里 medical 是「医疗的、医学的」（第 1 个义项：属于医疗职业与医学学科）；句意：她在车里放着医药箱，包里带着一份病历复印件。场景要点：一只白色药箱、一叠写满记录的纸、袋口露出的听诊器；对应第 1 个义项。

体检（英式口语，medical examination 的缩略）

senses.title: Of the profession
senses.titleCN: 医疗职业与学科：属于医生这一行
senses.definition: relating to the profession, practice or study of medicine
senses.definitionCN: 与医学职业、医疗实践或医学学科有关的
senses.example: She applied to three medical schools and was accepted by two.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了三所医学院，被其中两所录取。
senses.why: Medical entered English in the 1640s from Late Latin medicalis, 'of a physician', from medicus 'physician'. The adjective first names whatever belongs to doctors.
senses.whyCN: medical 于 17 世纪 40 年代从晚期拉丁语 medicalis 进入英语，意为“医生的”，源自 medicus“医生”。这个形容词最初用来命名一切属于医生的东西。

senses.title: Medical versus surgical
senses.titleCN: 内科的：与外科相对的那一半
senses.definition: relating to treatment by drugs and other non-surgical means, as opposed to surgery
senses.definitionCN: 指以药物及其他非手术手段进行的治疗，与外科相对
senses.example: He was moved from the surgical ward to the medical ward for observation.
senses.exampleCN: 他从外科病房转到内科病房接受观察。
senses.why: Inside one profession, medical marks the branch that treats with medicine rather than the knife. The word draws a line within the hospital, not outside it.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个行业内部，medical 标记的是用药物而不是用刀的那一支。这个词画的是医院内部的界线，而不是对外的界线。

senses.title: The patient's condition
senses.titleCN: 身体状况与病史：属于这个人的健康
senses.definition: relating to a person's health, illnesses and physical condition
senses.definitionCN: 与某人的健康、疾病和身体状况有关的
senses.example: The form asks for your medical history and any allergies.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表格要求填写你的病史和过敏情况。
senses.why: The adjective shifts from the profession to the patient: what belongs to the physician's domain becomes the record of a body's past.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从职业转到病人身上：原本属于医生领域的东西，变成了一个身体过往的记录。

senses.title: A medical: the check-up
senses.titleCN: 体检：形容词被剪成一个名词
senses.definition: a medical examination
senses.definitionCN: 体检；医学检查
senses.example: He passed his medical and joined the crew in March.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过了体检，三月加入了船员队伍。
senses.why: Recorded from 1917 as a shortening of medical examination. English often clips a familiar adjective-plus-noun phrase into the adjective alone.
senses.whyCN: 1917 年起有记录，是 medical examination 的缩略。英语常把熟悉的“形容词加名词”词组剪成只剩形容词。

senses.title: A medical: the doctor
senses.titleCN: 医学生、医生：旧时的口语名词
senses.definition: in older colloquial use, a medical student or a doctor
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中指医科学生或医生
senses.example: The old novels speak of a medical coming to the house at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 旧小说里常写一位医生半夜上门。
senses.why: The noun use is recorded from 1823. A person is named by what he or she studies or practises, so the adjective stands alone as a human subject.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法自 1823 年有记录。人被以他所学或所做的事来称呼，于是这个形容词单独站出来指人。

senses.title: Medical evidence
senses.titleCN: 法律与保险中的医学鉴定
senses.definition: used of reports, evidence and certificates that come from doctors and carry legal or official weight
senses.definitionCN: 指来自医生、具有法律或官方效力的报告、证据与证明
senses.example: The court ordered a medical report before deciding on the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在裁定索赔之前下令出具一份医学报告。
senses.why: Once medicine enters law, its documents become evidence. Medical marks the source of authority behind the paper.
senses.whyCN: 一旦医学进入法律，它的文书就成了证据。medical 标记的是这张纸背后的权威来源。

senses.title: Medical equipment
senses.titleCN: 器械与技术：复合词里的限定语
senses.definition: used in compounds for equipment, imaging and technology employed in health care
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，指医疗照护中使用的设备、影像与技术
senses.example: The charity shipped medical supplies and two portable ultrasound machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构运去了医疗物资和两台便携超声仪。
senses.why: As a classifying adjective it can attach to any object used in care, from a glove to a scanner, without changing its own meaning.
senses.whyCN: 作为分类形容词，它可以附着在任何用于照护的物件上，从手套到扫描仪，而自身含义不变。

senses.title: Medical leave
senses.titleCN: 病假与证明：制度里的一个类别
senses.definition: used in employment contexts for leave or certificates that excuse absence because of illness
senses.definitionCN: 用于雇佣语境，指因病请假或证明缺勤正当的证明文件
senses.example: She took five days of medical leave after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后她请了五天病假。
senses.why: Institutions need a word for absence backed by a doctor. Medical turns an illness into a recognised administrative category.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个词来指“有医生作保的缺勤”。medical 把一场病变成一个被承认的行政类别。

senses.title: Medical, not medicinal
senses.titleCN: 与 medicinal 的分界：说用途，不说药效
senses.definition: describing the setting or profession of health care, not the healing power of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 描述医疗的场景或职业，而不是某物质本身具有的治疗效力
senses.example: Medical use is the right phrase for a clinic; medicinal use describes a herb that actually heals.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所的用途该说医疗用途；而药用价值说的是某种草药确实能治病。
senses.why: Medicinal arrived first, in the mid-14th century, meaning 'having curative properties'. Medical came later and names the profession, so the pair divides into 'who treats' and 'what cures'.
senses.whyCN: medicinal 先到，14 世纪中叶就有，意为“具有治疗效力的”。medical 来得更晚，命名的是职业，于是这一对词分成“谁来治”与“什么能治”。

intro.en: Medical is a Latin adjective borrowed through French, built on medicus 'physician'. Its root means 'take appropriate measures', not 'middle', and it has no connection with method. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: medical 是经法语借入的拉丁语形容词，建立在 medicus“医生”之上。它的词根意为“采取恰当措施”，不是“中间”，并且与 method 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'pertaining to the art or profession of healing, or to those who practise it'. It came through French médical from Late Latin medicalis 'of a physician'.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 40 年代，意为“与治疗之术或行业、与行医者有关的”。它经法语 médical 来自晚期拉丁语 medicalis“医生的”。

items.en: Latin medicus was both a noun, 'physician, surgeon, medical man', and an adjective, 'healing, medicinal'. It comes from medeor 'to cure, heal', originally 'know the best course for'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 medicus 既是名词“医生、外科医生、医者”，也是形容词“治疗的、药用的”。它来自 medeor“治愈、治疗”，原义为“知道最好的做法”。

items.en: The root *med- means 'take appropriate measures'. De Vaan explains medeor as a shift from 'measure' to 'distribute a cure, heal'; Avestan vi-mad- 'physician' belongs to the same family.
items.cn: 词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”。de Vaan 把 medeor 解释为从“量度”转向“分配药剂、治疗”；阿维斯陀语 vi-mad-“医生”同属这一族。

items.en: The earlier English adjective in this sense was medicinal, 'having healing or curative properties', from Latin medicinalis. Medical later took over the professional sense.
items.cn: 英语中较早表示这一意义的形容词是 medicinal，即“有治疗或治愈效力的”，来自拉丁语 medicinalis。medical 后来接管了职业性的那一层意义。

items.en: The noun is recorded from 1823 colloquially for 'a medical student or practitioner', and from 1917 as a shortening of medical examination.
items.cn: 名词用法 1823 年起有口语记录，指“医科学生或医生”；1917 年起则是 medical examination（体检）的缩略。

items.en: Medical and method share only their letters. Method is Greek methodos, meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road'; no Latin medicus is involved. The -met- shape in the two words is a coincidence, and medicine (c. 1200) likewise comes from medicina, not from medical.
items.cn: medical 与 method 只共享字母外形。method 是希腊语 methodos，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，其中没有任何拉丁语 medicus 的成分。两个词里的 -met- 外形纯属巧合；medicine（约 1200 年）同样来自 medicina，而不是来自 medical。

note.en: The first group is the real medic- family: the substance, the healing property, the act of dosing, and the pills themselves. The second group compares adjectives used in and around health care.
note.cn: 第一组是真正的 medic- 词族：医学本身、治疗效力、用药动作、以及药片本身。第二组比较医疗领域内外的几个形容词。

entries.definition: the science and practice of treating disease, or a substance taken to treat illness. It is the thing and the field; medical is only the adjective that points at them.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗疾病的科学与实践，或用来治病的物质。它是事物与领域本身；medical 只是指向它们的形容词。

entries.definition: having curative properties, or used as a medicine. A medicinal herb heals; a medical herb is merely one a doctor might study.
entries.definitionCN: 具有治疗效力的，或作药用的。medicinal 的草药能治病；medical 的草药只是医生可能会研究的那种草。

entries.definition: to treat with medicine, or to add a drug to something. It names the act that medical describes only indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 用药物治疗，或往某物里加药。它命名的是 medical 只间接描述的那个动作。

entries.definition: a medicinal substance, or the treatment of a condition with drugs. Since 1942 it has been the everyday word for prescribed pills.
entries.definitionCN: 药物，或用药物处理某种病情。自 1942 年起，它成了“处方药”的日常说法。

entries.definition: relating to the observation and treatment of patients, or to a clinic. Clinical stresses the setting and the method; medical stresses the profession as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与病人的观察和治疗有关的，或与诊所相关的。clinical 强调场景与方法；medical 强调整个行业。

entries.definition: relating to the healing of disease, or having a calming or restorative effect. It is closer to medicinal than to medical.
entries.definitionCN: 与疾病治疗有关的，或有镇静、康复效果的。它更接近 medicinal，而不是 medical。

entries.definition: relating to surgery. It is the usual opposite of medical inside a hospital, where medical means treatment by drugs rather than by operation.
entries.definitionCN: 与外科手术有关的。在医院内部它常是 medical 的对立面，那里的 medical 指用药物治疗而非手术。

entries.definition: relating to the auxiliary services that support medical work, such as ambulance crews and lab technicians. The prefix para- 'beside' marks the supporting role.
entries.definitionCN: 与辅助医疗服务有关的，如救护人员与化验员。前缀 para-“在旁边”标记的是支持性的角色。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin medicus 'physician', mederi 'to heal', the older adjective medicinal, and the modern family medicine, medication, medic.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 medicus“医生”、mederi“治疗”、更早的形容词 medicinal，以及现代的 medicine、medication、medic 词族。

normal.en: medic- means 'physician'. Medical is simply the adjective of the doctor's world, as in medical school and medical records.
normal.cn: medic- 表示“医生”。medical 就是医生那个世界的形容词，如 medical school（医学院）、medical records（病历）。

normal.en: The deeper root *med- means 'take appropriate measures'. Healing began as the art of knowing the right measure.
normal.cn: 更深的词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”。治疗最初就是“知道该用多少分量”的技艺。

normal.en: medicinal is older and means 'having healing power'; medical is younger and means 'of the profession'. A medicinal plant heals, a medical student studies.
normal.cn: medicinal 更老，意为“有治疗效力的”；medical 更年轻，意为“属于这一行业的”。药草能治病，医学生则在读书。

normal.en: A medical (noun) is a check-up: the adjective swallowed the noun examination in 1917.
normal.cn: 名词 a medical 就是体检：1917 年这个形容词把名词 examination 吞掉了。

normal.en: Method looks similar but is Greek: meta plus hodos 'road'. Medical has no road in it, only a physician.
normal.cn: method 看着像，其实是希腊语：meta 加 hodos“路”。medical 里面没有路，只有一个医生。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat with two pockets: one holds a stethoscope, the other a folder of records. The coat is medical; the herb in the garden is medicinal.
abstract.cn: 想象一件白大褂有两个口袋：一个装听诊器，一个装一叠病历。这件外套是 medical；园子里的那株草药是 medicinal。

abstract.en: The word always points at people and their apparatus, never at the power of a plant. That is why a hospital is medical and a cough syrup is medicinal.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是指向人及其器械，从不指向植物的效力。所以医院是 medical，止咳糖浆是 medicinal。

abstract.en: A whole institution hides behind three syllables: school, ward, record, certificate, leave. Each is a room the adjective has learned to enter.
abstract.cn: 三个音节背后藏着一整套机构：学院、病房、病历、证明、病假。每一个都是这个形容词学会进入的房间。

examples.en: The village has no medical staff, only a nurse who comes twice a week.
examples.cn: 这个村子没有医务人员，只有一名每周来两次的护士。

examples.en: The insurance company asked for the medical report before paying.
examples.cn: 保险公司在付款前要求提供医学报告。

examples.en: She was on medical leave for a month and came back thinner and quieter.
examples.cn: 她休了一个月病假，回来时瘦了，也沉默了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦迪扣”——麦迪把白大褂的扣子扣好，口袋里插着听诊器 → medical 医疗的、医学的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 medicus“医生”与 mederi“治疗”，词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”，核心是“为身体采取正确的救治手段”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of medical, all radiating from one point: whatever belongs to the physician's world — the school, the ward, the record, the certificate, the machine — and finally the patient's own body as that world describes it.
sensesIntro.cn: medical 的九个义项都从一个点辐射出去：一切属于医生世界的东西——学院、病房、病历、证明、机器——最后是那个世界所描述的病人身体本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white coat whose pockets hold a stethoscope and a folder of records.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件白大褂，口袋里装着听诊器和一叠病历。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: medical names the field and also the drug-treating half of it, set against surgery.
branches.cn: 行业：medical 命名这一领域，也命名其中用药治疗的那一半，与外科相对。

branches.en: THE BODY: the adjective moves from doctors to the patient, naming health, illness and history.
branches.cn: 身体：这个形容词从医生移到病人身上，命名健康、疾病与病史。

branches.en: CLIPPED NOUNS: English shortens 'medical examination' to a medical, and once shortened 'medical man' to the same form.
branches.cn: 截短名词：英语把 medical examination 缩成 a medical，也曾把 medical man 缩成同一个形式。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: law, insurance and employment turn medical into documents, evidence and leave.
branches.cn: 制度：法律、保险与雇佣把 medical 变成文书、证据与病假。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND BOUNDARY: the adjective classifies equipment, and stops short of medicinal, which describes healing power rather than professional setting.
branches.cn: 物件与边界：这个形容词为器械分类，同时止步于 medicinal——后者描述治疗效力，而不是职业场景。

intro.en: Medical is Latin medicus plus the adjective ending -alis, softened in English to -al. The stem medic- is not a free English word, but it carries the whole family.
intro.cn: medical 是拉丁语 medicus 加形容词词尾 -alis，进入英语后软化为 -al。词干 medic- 在英语里不能单独成词，却撑起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin medicus 'physician' and mederi 'to heal' go back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures'. Latin medicina gave English medicine; medicinalis gave medicinal; medicatio gave medication. There is no Greek element in medical.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medicus“医生”与 mederi“治疗”可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当措施”。拉丁语 medicina 给出英语 medicine；medicinalis 给出 medicinal；medicatio 给出 medication。medical 里没有任何希腊语成分。

items.meaning: of or relating to medicine and physicians
items.meaningCN: 医疗的；医学的（medic- 医生 + -al 形容词词尾）
items.example: The medical team arrived before the ambulances.
items.exampleCN: 医疗队在救护车之前就到了。

items.meaningCN: 医学；医术；药物（-ine 构成名词）
items.example: Medicine has changed more in thirty years than in three centuries.
items.exampleCN: 医学在三十年里的变化超过了过去三个世纪。

items.example: The root has a medicinal taste that children hate.
items.exampleCN: 这种根有孩子讨厌的药味。

items.meaningCN: 用药物治疗；给……用药（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The water is medicated with chlorine.

items.meaning: treatment with drugs; a medicinal substance
items.meaningCN: 药物治疗；药物（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: He takes his medication after breakfast.

items.meaning: in medical terms; from a medical point of view
items.meaningCN: 从医学上讲（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 这种情况在医学上无法解释。

items.meaning: a doctor, student of medicine, or battlefield medical orderly
items.meaningCN: 医生；医学生；战地卫生员（截短词干）
items.example: A medic stopped the bleeding at the roadside.
items.exampleCN: 一名卫生员在路边止住了血。

items.meaning: relating to biology and medicine together
items.meaningCN: 生物医学的（bio- 生命 + medical）
items.example: The lab won a grant for biomedical research.
items.exampleCN: 该实验室获得了生物医学研究的资助。

items.meaning: supporting medical work without being a doctor
items.meaningCN: 辅助医疗的（para- 在旁边 + medical）
items.example: Paramedical staff handle the first response.

definition_zh: 学院；大学；（英国）公学
definition_en: a school where students study after secondary school, or part of a university
core_image: 中学之后继续读书的校园
scene: 哥哥收到录取信，全家都为他的大学开心。 His dream is to study engineering at a good college.
sceneCN: 这里 college 是「学院；大学」（第 1 个义项：中学后的高等学校）；句意是他梦想在一所好学院学工程。

derivatives.zh: 由 college 加后缀构成，义为「学院的；大学的」
来自同一拉丁词根，义为「同事」

senses.title: A school after secondary school
senses.definition: a place where students study a subject after finishing secondary school
senses.definitionCN: 中学生毕业后继续学习的地方
senses.example: After senior high, Li Hua will go to college.
senses.exampleCN: 高中毕业后，李华将去上大学。
senses.why: The word names the next school up the ladder, where study becomes deeper.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指阶梯上更高一级的学校，学习内容更深。

senses.title: A part of a university
senses.definition: one of the parts inside a university, often with its own buildings and teachers
senses.definitionCN: 大学内部的组成部分，往往有独立的楼舍与师资
senses.example: Each college of the university has its own dining hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大学的每个学院都有自己的食堂。
senses.why: A big university splits into smaller houses so students feel at home.
senses.whyCN: 大大学分成小院落，让学生更有归属感，于是有了这个义项。

senses.title: A group with one job or duty
senses.definition: a group of people who share one profession or duty, such as an election college
senses.definitionCN: 承担同一职业或职责的人群，如选举团
senses.example: The election college meets to choose the president.
senses.exampleCN: 选举团开会选出总统。
senses.why: People who trained together were once called a college, so the word reached organised groups.
senses.whyCN: 曾经一起受过训练的人被称为 college，这个词便用到了有组织的团体上。

intro.en: College began as a word for people bound together, not buildings.
intro.cn: college 起初指「结合在一起的人」，而不是楼房。

items.en: Latin collega meant a person chosen to work with another, a partner in office.
items.cn: 拉丁语 collega 指被选出来与他人共事的人，即同僚。

items.en: Latin colligium later meant a body or society of such partners.
items.cn: 拉丁语 colligium 后来指这类人组成的团体。

items.en: Old French college meant an association or league of people.
items.cn: 古法语 college 指人的社团或联合会。

items.en: Middle English college first named groups of priests living under one roof.
items.cn: 中古英语 college 最初指住在同一屋檐下的教士团体。

items.en: Modern English college moved from religious groups to schools for higher study.
items.cn: 现代英语 college 从教士团体转指高等教育学校。

note.en: The first group collects same-root words; the second collects other schools above secondary level.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词，第二组收中学以上的其他学校。

entries.definition: A picture made of many pieces stuck together.

entries.definition: Relating to a college.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学院的」，是 college 的形容词形式。

entries.definition: The highest school for study and research.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学」，规模通常比 college 更大。

entries.definition: A school for a special subject.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专科院校；学会」。

entries.definition: A school or body for special study.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院；研究所」。

normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁「同僚」本义与校园生活记 college。

normal.en: colleague and college share the Latin root.
normal.cn: colleague 与 college 同一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: Many students say go to college.
normal.cn: 很多学生说 go to college。

normal.en: A university can contain many colleges.

normal.en: College life starts with a campus card.

abstract.en: Picture partners walking through one gate together.
abstract.cn: 想象同窗伙伴一起走过同一扇校门。

abstract.en: See small houses inside a huge campus.
abstract.cn: 想象大学校园里的一座座小院。

abstract.en: Think of a ladder: middle school, then college.
abstract.cn: 想一架梯子：中学，然后是学院。

examples.en: My sister is a college student in Shanghai.
examples.cn: 我姐姐是上海的一名大学生。

examples.en: They worked hard so they could go to college together.
examples.cn: 他们努力学习，为的是能一起上大学。

examples.en: Our school team plays against the college team on Sunday.
examples.cn: 周日我们校队与学院队比赛。
